title: Bijecting $m$-Tamari intervals, trees, and tight gradings
summary: Tight gradings, which are certain integer gradings on maximal Dyck paths, provide a combinatorial framework for computing all coefficients of wall-functions in rank-$2$ cluster scattering diagrams. We construct a bijection between a special subset of tight gradings and the intervals of the $m$-Tamari lattice, providing a new combinatorial proof of the central wall-function formula proved by Reineke. Inspired by the structure of these gradings, we introduce a class of plane trees called $m$-leafy trees that give a new model for $m$-Tamari intervals. The defining condition of an $m$-leafy tree is simple: in every full subtree, the number of leaves is greater than $m$ times the number of internal vertices. The leafy tree perspective gives rise to a quadratic functional equation with a catalytic parameter, providing an alternative way to enumerate $m$-Tamari intervals.

title: Questions of minimality for DDMOGs and cycle ornaments
summary: Difference distance magic oriented graphs (DDMOGs) are oriented graphs whose vertices admit a bijective labeling by consecutive positive integers such that every vertex has weight zero, where the weight is the sum of the labels of its in-neighbors minus the sum of the labels of its out-neighbors. We investigate minimality and sparsity questions for DDMOGs and their ornaments. First, we develop new constructions of cycle-based ornaments that reduce the number of cycles required for a given number of attachment nodes and identify minimal cycle lengths in several cases. Second, we determine the minimum number of arcs in a nontrivial DDMOG of order $n$, combining computational enumeration for small orders with theoretical lower bounds and constructions. Langford sequences provide a key tool in these constructions, enabling us to partition consecutive labels into difference triples and thereby construct sparse DDMOGs. Finally, we use related constructions to obtain generalized ornaments with no internal arcs. These results advance the study of minimal constructions in difference distance magic labeling and provide new methods for building sparse DDMOGs.

title: Brown-Gap Healing and Exact Completeness Thresholds for Leading-Unit Positive Linear Recurrences
summary: We determine the exact completeness threshold for standard positive linear recurrence sequences whose coefficient lists consist of leading units, followed by zeros and a final positive coefficient. Using the generating function of Brown's gaps, we prove a necessary and sufficient condition for completeness, including the boundary case in which the critical gap vanishes. We further establish strict monotonicity of the unrounded threshold in the number of leading units, thereby resolving the corresponding leading-unit monotonicity conjecture.

title: Bulgarian solitaire with distinguishable cells
summary: Classical Bulgarian solitaire tracks only the sizes of the stacks. We ask how the lengths of its periodic orbits change when individual cards are distinguished. To study this question, we introduce four actions $T_1,T_2,T_3,T_4$ on partitions with labeled cells. The actions differ in whether the top or bottom cell is removed from each column and in the order in which the removed cells are arranged to form a new column. We determine the exact sizes of the periodic orbits for all four actions. The main work lies in the analysis of $T_2$, for which we develop a coloring algorithm on Ferrers diagrams. The coloring encodes the cycle structure of the permutation of the labels induced by one full period of the underlying partition.

title: On the structural aspects of Convex Subhyperlattices under different orders
summary: Nayak et al. (2025) introduced the concept of convex subhyperlattices of a strong join hyperlattice $\mathfrak{L}$ and demonstrated that the collection of all convex subhyperlattices, $\operatorname{CS}(\mathfrak{L})$, together with empty set, forms a lattice. In particular, for $P$-hyperlattices and Nakano hyperlattices, they obtained a unique representation of convex subhyperlattices in terms of hyperideals and hyperfilters. In the present work, we extend these studies by proving that $\operatorname{CS}(\mathfrak{L}) \cup \{\emptyset\}$, under set inclusion, forms an algebraic lattice. Moreover, we introduce two new orders on $\operatorname{CS}(\mathfrak{L})$ and examine their properties, including conditions for equivalence of these orders. In the class of $P$-hyperlattices, we characterize convex subhyperlattices in terms of initial and final segments, providing a structural insight into their formation. When convexity is extended to arbitrary join hyperlattices, many results known for $P$-hyperlattices and Nakano hyperlattices fail to hold. To address these limitations of convexity in arbitrary hyperlattices, we introduce the notion of strongly convex sets, denoted $\operatorname{SC}(\mathfrak{L})$, which naturally generalizes the concept while preserving its fundamental properties and extends the applicability of results to a wider setting. We establish several results for $\operatorname{SC}(\mathfrak{L})$ that do not hold for $\operatorname{CS}(\mathfrak{L})$.

title: The cofinite regularity spectrum of $F$-irregular graphs
summary: For a connected graph $F$, a graph $G$ is $F$-irregular if the numbers of copies of $F$ containing its vertices are pairwise distinct. We characterize which connected patterns admit regular $F$-irregular hosts of every sufficiently large degree. Stars admit no regular $F$-irregular host; for every other $F$, every sufficiently large integer $r$ is realized by a connected $r$-regular $F$-irregular graph of diameter two and order $r+o(r)$, optimal to first order. For triangles, and equivalently four-vertex paths in regular graphs, we construct such hosts of order less than $r+73r^{\log29/\log58}$ above an explicit threshold, with the constant reduced to $44$ for even $r$. Lexicographic words encode distinct rooted subgraph counts, while layered connections allow the common degree to be prescribed. Rooted-homomorphism expansions and spectral amplification establish separation for general patterns; an exact uniform-increment identity gives the quantitative triangle construction. The finite seed graphs are explicitly constructed, and their required rooted-count distinctions are verified by exact-arithmetic certificates.

title: A Lie-theoretic approach to the type $C_n^{(1)}$ partitions of Capparelli, Meurman, Primc and Primc
summary: Capparelli, Meurman, Primc and Primc (CMPP) extended the frequency conditions in Gordon's partition theorem to paths in coloured arrays. Their conjecture for type $C_n^{(1)}$ identifies the generating function of admissible arrays with a principally specialized character. We prove this conjecture for arbitrary boundary data by constructing an ordered Poincaré--Birkhoff--Witt (PBW) basis of the corresponding integrable highest weight module. A decomposition of the admissible arrays and a tensor product argument establish linear independence of the corresponding monomial vectors. To prove spanning, we use relations from annihilating fields and PBW bases for modules over finite Levi subalgebras. Principal specialization then yields the conjectured product. The same basis identifies the number of parts with the degree in the associated graded module for the PBW filtration.

title: The $ν$-core label order and noncrossing partitions
summary: We prove that the poset of $s$-noncrossing partitions is isomorphic to the core label order of the $ν$-Tamari lattice introduced by Préville-Ratelle and Viennot.

title: A 43-vertex 4-chromatic unit-distance graph in the plane with girth 5
summary: We exhibit a set of 43 points in the Euclidean plane whose unit-distance graph has 83 edges, girth 5 and chromatic number 4. The smallest previously known 4-chromatic unit-distance graph of girth 5, due to Hochberg and O'Donnell (1996), has 45 vertices. The new graph is 4-critical, has trivial automorphism group, and has exactly 2n-3 edges; it is a Laman graph and its unit-distance realisation is infinitesimally rigid. The coordinates are algebraic numbers, specified as the unique real solution of an explicit system of 82 quadratic equations inside an explicit rational box. Every claim is certified by exact computation: existence and uniqueness of the realisation by a rational contraction-mapping certificate (independently re-checked with interval Krawczyk arithmetic), and non-3-colourability both by exhaustive search and by a DRAT proof verified with drat-trim.

title: On maximum volume polytopes inscribed in the sphere
summary: We combine degree sequence bounds with a supporting tangent plane method to study maximum volume polytopes inscribed in the sphere $\mathbb S^2$. Building on the vertex-star estimates and combinatorial reductions in Wimmer's dissertation, we determine the exact maximum for ten vertices and the unique maximizing combinatorial type for eleven vertices. Moreover, using explicit computational certificates we identify a unique possible maximizing type for polytopes with thirteen and fifteen vertices, and two possible types for sixteen vertices; this approach also recovers Wimmer's fourteen-vertex combinatorial theorem. Finally, we derive a facial inequality which holds for every degree pattern, and prove that the maximum volume for polytopes with thirty-two vertices is $\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{10(5-\sqrt{5})}$, attained precisely by an inscribed realization of the pentakis dodecahedron, which is the convex hull of the regular icosahedron together with its normalized facet centers. Wimmer had already determined this configuration and its optimality within its own combinatorial type. We also obtain a global degree sequence envelope and a universal affine volume bound.

title: Spectral distribution for biased orientations of random graphs
summary: We study the Hermitian adjacency matrix of the second kind for biased orientations of Erdos-Renyi random graphs. In the model $D(n,p,p')$, an edge is present with probability $p$ and, conditional on its presence, is directed from its smaller to its larger endpoint with probability $p'$. Both parameters may depend on $n$, and biased tournaments are the special case $D(n,1,p')$. We prove a global semicircle law whenever $n(p(1-p)+3p^2p'(1-p')) \to \infty$, for both the centered and the uncentered matrix, and also for the expected empirical spectral measure. Our second theorem gives the exact spectrum of the mean matrix and the limits of the extreme eigenvalues on the scale $np$, under a sufficient density assumption. The main difference from the unbiased random orientations (where $p'=1/2$) is emergence of multiple large eigenvalues. The proofs include the closed-walk counting, control of the moment variances, an explicit diagonalization of the deterministic bias, and the passage from centered to uncentered spectral measures.

title: The Brualdi--Quinn conjecture on strong edge-coloring holds fractionally and asymptotically
summary: Let $G$ be a bipartite graph with parts $A$ and $B$, and let $Δ_A$ and $Δ_B$ be the maximum degrees of the vertices in $A$ and in $B$, respectively. Brualdi and Quinn conjectured that the strong chromatic index of $G$ is at most $Δ_AΔ_B$. We prove that the fractional strong chromatic index of $G$ is at most $Δ_AΔ_B$, and that the conjecture holds asymptotically: $χ_s'(G)\le(1+o(1))Δ_AΔ_B$ as $\max\{Δ_A,Δ_B\}\to\infty$. The error term is $12(\lnΔ)^{1/2}Δ^{-1/4}$ with $Δ=\max\{Δ_A,Δ_B\}$. Both results rest on a smart partition of edges and Lovász Local Lemma.

title: Vertex splitting, global rigidity and nondegenerate equilibrium stresses
summary: We prove Whiteley's conjecture that every nontrivial vertex split of a generically globally rigid graph preserves generic global rigidity in \(\mathbb{R}^d\), for all \(d\geq1\). We give two proofs of the stronger assertion that the split graph is infinitesimally rigid at every generic coincident realisation of the two split vertices. Both proofs use maximum-rank equilibrium stress matrices and then apply the coincident-rigidity criterion of Cruickshank, Jackson and Tanigawa. The second construction also shows that every generically globally rigid graph admits a nondegenerate equilibrium stress of maximum rank at every generic realisation, establishing a conjecture of Jordán and Tanigawa.

title: Dominant permutations, positive mixed-variable formulas, and product-splitting equivalence for (double) Schubert polynomials
summary: We present new positive combinatorial formulas for triple Schubert coefficients in mixed-variable products of double Schubert polynomials, $\mathfrak{S}_u(x;y)\mathfrak{S}_v(x;z)$, expressed in the $\mathfrak{S}_w(x;y)$ basis, in the case where $u$ is dominant. This result complements earlier results where $v$ was assumed dominant. To generalize further, we introduce a relation on permutations that we call ``domination,'' under which dominant permutations dominate all others. When $u$ dominates $w$, we obtain an explicit positive formula for $c^w_{u,v}(y;z)$, which in particular yields positivity when $u$ and $v$ have separated descents. In addition to these new positivity results, we establish a product--splitting equivalence for double Schubert polynomials, relating triple Schubert coefficients to splitting coefficients. This equivalence highlights structural symmetries and provides reduction methods for computing coefficients that are otherwise difficult to access. Taken together, these results extend the range of double Schubert polynomial products for which positivity can be established combinatorially and yield explicit formulas that can be implemented computationally.

title: On the connected zero forcing polynomial of finite trees
summary: Given a graph $Γ$ with vertex set $V(Γ)$ and a set of colored vertices S, the zero forcing rule is an iterative graph coloring process which states that a colored vertex with exactly one uncolored neighbor forces that neighbor to become colored. If repeated application of this rule eventually colors every vertex of $Γ$, the set $S$ is called a \emph{zero forcing set}. Now, if the induced subgraph $Γ\vert_S$ is connected, then $S$ is called a \textit{connected zero forcing set}. The minimum cardinality of such a set is the \emph{connected zero forcing number} $Z_C(Γ)$. A \emph{connected zero forcing polynomial} of a finite graph $Γ$ is a monic polynomial $Z_C^Γ(x) \;=\; \sum_{k} a_k x^k$, where $a_k$ counts the number of connected zero forcing sets of $Γ$ of size $k$, which we denote by $Z_C(Γ,k)$. In this paper, we find the connected zero forcing polynomial of any finite tree $T$. We then establish sharp lower bounds for each coefficient of the connected zero forcing polynomial, over all trees on $n$ vertices with $p$ many pendant vertices. We also identify a family of trees, which we call uniform trees, and we prove that for any tree on $n$ vertices and $p$ many pendant vertices, there exists a uniform tree on $n$ vertices and $p$ many pendant vertices, whose connected zero forcing polynomial bounds as an upper bound, the connected zero forcing polynomial of the tree coefficient wise. Again for $2\leq p\leq 4$, we establish a sharp upper bound for each coefficient of the connected zero forcing polynomial, over all trees on $n$ vertices with $p$ many pendant vertices.

title: Non-log-concave $τ$-polynomials of regular graphs
summary: For any simple graph $G$ on $n$ vertices, write its chromatic polynomial in the rising factorial basis as $P(G,x)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}(-1)^{n-j}c_j x^{\langle j\rangle}$, where $x^{\langle j\rangle}=\prod_{i=0}^{j-1}(x+i)$ for any $j\ge 1$ and $x^{\langle0\rangle}=1$. Brenti (1992) introduced the $τ$-polynomial and its augmented version, defined by $$τ(G,x)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}c_jx^j, \qquad \overlineτ(G,x)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}j!c_jx^j.$$ He asked whether $τ(G,x)$ always has only real roots and whether $\overlineτ(G,x)$ always has a log-concave coefficient sequence. In this paper, we show that for any integer $d\ge 4$, there exists an integer $h_d$ such that, for every connected $d$-regular graph $G$ of girth at least $h_d$, the coefficient sequence of $τ(G,x)$ fails to be log-concave. This failure also occurs for $\overlineτ(G,x)$, and Newton's inequalities imply that $τ(G,x)$ has nonreal roots. Thus both questions have counterexamples among regular graphs of arbitrarily large girth.

title: Lower bound on the size of splitting systems
summary: For even $t$ and an $n$-set $X$, an $(n,t)$-splitting system is a family ${\mathbb{B}} \subseteq 2^X$ with the property that for each subset $Y \in {X \choose t}$, there exists $B \in \mathbb{B}$ such that $|B \cap Y| = t/2$. The problem of interest is to determine the minimum size of such splitting systems. We show that any $(n,t)$-splitting system has size at least of order $t$, improving the previous lower bound of $\sqrt t$ while the best known upper bound is of order $t^{3/2}$.

title: Triangle-overlap cores and density bounds for Tuza's conjecture
summary: For a finite simple graph $G$, let $ν(G)$ be the maximum number of edge-disjoint triangles and let $τ(G)$ be the minimum number of edges meeting every triangle. We prove $τ(G)\le2ν(G)$ when each edge belongs to at most four triangles, the edges belonging to four triangles form components with at most two edges, and the maximum average degree is at most $25/2$. No upper bound on maximum vertex degree is imposed. We also localize the density condition. Let $K$ be the Hifumi core, defined as the vertex set of the 4-core of the spanning subgraph formed by edges belonging to at least three triangles. It suffices to impose the density condition on $G[K]$, including all original edges between vertices of $K$. More generally, when the four-triangle edges have maximum degree at most two, reductions produce a subgraph $R\subseteq G[K]$ with $τ(G)-2ν(G)\leτ(R)-2ν(R)$. Consequently an empty core gives a density-free sufficient condition. For the first graph class, a quantitative surplus argument strengthens both the global and localized density conditions to the strict bound $25/2+2/56775$. The proof combines edge reductions, discharging, finite certificates and a weak König--Egerváry lemma for links of arbitrary order. The general conjecture and the removal of the density condition from the first graph class remain unresolved here.

title: The $(t-1)$-chromatic Ramsey number of cycles for three colours
summary: For integers $t\ge 2$ and $\ell\ge 3$, let $R^t_{t-1}(C_\ell)$ be the least integer $n$ such that every colouring of the edges of $K_n$ with $t$ colours contains a cycle of length $\ell$ whose edges use at most $t-1$ colours. Bucić and Khamseh determined the analogous number for paths and asked for its value for cycles. We answer this question for three colours: we show that $R^3_2(C_\ell)=\ell+\lfloor(\ell+1)/6\rfloor$ for every $\ell\ge 11$, and we determine the values for $3\le \ell\le 10$.

title: Token graphs of stars
summary: The $k$-token graph $F_k(G)$ of a graph $G$ has as vertices the $k$-subsets of $V(G)$, two of them being adjacent when their symmetric difference is an edge of $G$. Let $S_n$ be the star with $n$ leaves. Since every edge of $S_n$ is incident with the center, $F_k(S_n)$ is the inclusion graph of the $(k-1)$- and the $k$-subsets of the leaves. We use this identification to determine its diameter, radius, girth, Wiener index and number of spanning trees, and to decompose $F_k(S_{n+1})$ into $F_k(S_n)$ and $F_{k-1}(S_n)$ joined by a matching; the parameters of $F_k(S_n)$ that are already known, such as its connectivity, independence number, automorphism group and spectrum, are collected in an appendix. The two parameters that the identification does not settle are the domination and the packing numbers. For the domination number we prove, for fixed $k \ge 3$, that $(1-\frac{k-2}{k-1}π_k-o(1))\binom{n}{k-1} \le γ(F_k(S_n)) \le (1-\frac{1}{2}(\frac{k-2}{k-1})^{k-2}+o(1))\binom{n}{k-1}$, where $π_k$ is the Turan density of the complete $(k-1)$-uniform hypergraph on $k$ vertices; for $k=3$ both constants are equal to $\frac{3}{4}$, so that $γ(F_3(S_n))=(\frac{3}{4}+o(1))\binom{n}{2}$, and the upper bound takes the exact form $γ(F_3(S_n)) \le \binom{n}{2}-\lfloor (n+1)^2/8 \rfloor$, which is attained for all $3 \le n \le 10$. For $k=4$ we improve the upper bound to $(\frac{17}{27}+o(1))\binom{n}{3}$, which matches the lower bound if Turan's conjecture $π_4=\frac{5}{9}$ holds. We show that the packing number of $F_k(S_n)$ equals the maximum size $A(n+1,4,k)$ of a binary constant-weight code, and we characterize when the packing and the domination numbers coincide, namely, for $2 \le k \le n-1$, exactly when $n=2k-1$ and a Steiner system $S(k-2,k-1,2k-1)$ exists; in that case both parameters equal the Catalan number $C_k$.

title: Weak Dissolution of Groups for Rearrangement
summary: Suppose that $k$ of $n$ classrooms are to be dissolved and their students moved to the other classrooms so that the numbers of students in any two remaining classrooms differ by at most $d$. We give a necessary and sufficient condition on the numbers of students for this to be possible whichever $k$ classrooms are dissolved. Moreover, we determine how small the largest classroom can be when this is possible. In particular, when all classrooms have different sizes, the smallest possible size of the largest classroom is $d+\lceil (n-d-1)(n-d)/(2k)\rceil$ if $k<(n-d-1)/2$, and it is $n$ or $n+1$ otherwise. This extends the results of Siriseriwan and Sripatak, who studied the case $d=0$.

title: Independence number and odd dominating models
summary: A dominating $K_t$-model, introduced by Illingworth and Wood [J. Graph Theory, 2025], is a sequence $(T_1,\dots,T_t)$ of pairwise vertex-disjoint subtrees of $G$ such that every vertex of $T_j$ has a neighbour in $T_i$ for $1\leq i<j\leq t$. Let $\text{had}_{\text{d}}(G)$ denote the maximum order of such a model. We prove two dominating-model analogues of improvements to the classical Duchet-Meyniel bound [Ann. Discrete Math., 1982]. The first extends a result of Kawarabayashi, Plummer, and Toft [J. Combin. Theory Ser. B, 2005]. Every $n$-vertex graph $G$ with $α(G)\geq2$ satisfies $\text{had}_{\text{d}}(G)\geq(n+ω(G))/(2α(G)-1)$. Second, we prove a constant-factor improvement of the Duchet-Meyniel bound for dominating models: every graph $G$ satisfies $\text{had}_{\text{d}}(G)>0.51075n/α(G)$. This qualitatively extends the results of Fox [SIAM J. Discrete Math., 2010] and Balogh and Kostochka [Discrete Math., 2011]. An odd dominating $K_t$-model is a dominating $K_t$-model with an assignment of one of two colours to each vertex of $V(T_1)\cup\dots\cup V(T_t)$, such that every edge of each $T_i$ is bichromatic and, for $1\leq i<j\leq t$, some edge between $T_i$ and $T_j$ is monochromatic. Let $\text{had}_{\text{od}}(G)$ denote the maximum order of such a model. Our constant-factor improvement of the Duchet-Meyniel bound relies on our next result: every claw-free graph $G$ satisfies $\text{had}_{\text{od}}(G)\geq 2χ(G)/3$, generalising a result of Chudnovsky and Fradkin [J. Graph Theory, 2010]. The factor 2/3 is asymptotically best possible. For $t\geq2$, we prove that every $n$-vertex graph with no odd dominating $K_t$-model has independence number at least $(n+t-1)/(2t-2)$. For the stronger notion in which every vertex of $T_j$ has a neighbour of the same colour in $T_i$, we prove the analogous results with $(n+t-1)/(2t-2)$ replaced by $(n+t-1)/(3t-3)$.

title: On the Kőnig-Egerváry theorem for $k$-trees
summary: The famous Kőnig-Egerváry theorem is equivalent to the statement that a graph is bipartite if and only if the matching number equals the vertex cover number for every induced subgraph. Bessy, Ochem, and Rautenbach (J. Graph Theory 91 (2019) 73-87) generalized this theorem to $k$-paths by introducing the class $\mathcal{G}_k$ of graphs where, for every induced subgraph, the maximum number of disjoint paths of order $k$ equals the minimum number of vertices intersecting all such paths. They provided complete structural characterizations of graphs in $\mathcal{G}_k$ for $k \in \{3, 4\}$, and for odd $k$ when no cycle of order less than $k$ is present. Inspired by this nice work, we extend the Kőnig-Egerváry theorem to $k$-trees (i.e., trees with exactly $k$ vertices). We define the class $\mathcal{J}_k$ of graphs where, for every induced subgraph, the maximum number of disjoint trees of order $k$ equals the minimum number of vertices intersecting all such trees, and provide complete structural descriptions of graphs in $\mathcal{J}_k$ for all $k \ge 3$.

title: Support enumerators of two-row grids and comb posets
summary: We enumerate lattice points of preorder polytopes by support size for two-row Ferrers posets and recursively defined comb posets. For two-row posets, the order-ideal inequalities give a reflected-walk model in the nonnegative quadrant. Its transfer operators have a rank-one commutator, from which we derive an identity with five independent parameters. A matching-parameter specialization factors into the enumerators of a Motzkin excursion and a Motzkin bridge and proves the conjectured product of type~A and type~B Narayana polynomials for a two-row grid with its maximum removed. The general identity also records the two row supports separately. For combs, maximum ideal excess leads to a scalar recursion and a cubic generating function with independent spine and tooth weights. This proves a compositional-inverse conjecture of Athanasiadis and Chapoton and gives explicit $γ$-coefficients by Lagrange inversion. We prove $γ$-positivity for all two-row Ferrers cell posets and for the combs. The truncated-grid enumerators have simple negative zeros.

title: Impropriety and resilience of the chromatic number
summary: We show that, for $p$ bounded away from $1$ and $np\to\infty$, the chromatic number of the binomial random graph $G_{n,p}$ is resilient to removal of a subgraph $H$ with $o(n \log(np))$ edges. It follows that the same assertion holds with $H$ being a subgraph of maximum degree $o(\log(np))$; and both these results are best possible up to a constant factor. We also prove corresponding results for the random $r$-regular graph $G_{n,r}$, when $r\to\infty$ and $r/n$ is bounded away from $1$, where $H$ has $o(n\log r)$ edges or maximum degree $o(\log r)$. Our results rely on a natural connection between chromatic resilience to edge removal and improper graph colouring. This work provides counterpoint to the work of Sudakov and Vu (2008) and Alon and Sudakov (2010), which treated chromatic resilience for $G_{n,p}$ subject to the addition, rather than removal, of edges.

title: Monk and Pieri rules for forest polynomials
summary: This article gives Pieri rules for forest polynomials and Monk rule for double forest polynomials. We construct binary relations $\lessdot_i$ and $\prec_i$ based on the local Tamari moves on indexed forests. These relations are explicit and constructive. For ordinary forest polynomials, the $h$- and $e$-Pieri rules are given by all chains of a fixed length along the cover relations, with certain restriction on the left or right endpoints. For double forest polynomials, our Monk rule shows every off-diagonal degree-one structure coefficient is always a single positive root, whose weight is also controlled by Tamari moves. Additionally, we introduce an insertion algorithm on positive injective words that yields a Monk rule for the corresponding slide polynomials. Regrouping this rule along Sylvester classes gives an independent Monk rule for ordinary forest polynomials.

title: Extremal graphs for Alon's graph coupon-collector conjecture
summary: Let \(G\) be a finite simple graph without isolated vertices. Starting with every vertex uncovered, at each step sample a vertex uniformly and independently and cover one of its uncovered neighbors, chosen uniformly, if any. Let \(\cc(G)\) denote the expected number of steps required to cover all vertices. Alon conjectured that disjoint unions of \(K_{d+1}\) maximize \(\cc(G)\) among \(d\)-regular graphs of a prescribed order whenever such unions exist. In this paper, we disprove this conjecture for every fixed \(d\ge2\) and give a complete characterization of the extremal graphs for \(d=2\) at every order \(n\ge3\). In particular, all but at most six vertices of any such extremal graph lie in four-cycle components.

title: Zero forcing is not unimodal
summary: The zero forcing polynomial of a graph counts the number of distinct zero forcing sets of every possible size. In 2018, Boyer et al. asked whether the zero forcing polynomial is always unimodal, and provided some evidence that it is. We answer this question by constructing an infinite family of graphs whose zero forcing polynomials are not unimodal. Our construction also shows that the graph polynomials associated with connected forcing and total forcing are also not unimodal in general.

title: Tiling of Hyperbolic Surface by Maximal Number of Tiles
summary: Tilings of a closed hyperbolic surface by congruent $n$-gons with $n\ge 7$ is a finite problem. One extreme of the finite problem is that the number of tiles is maximal. The problem is related to edge-to-edge tilings of the Poincaré disk ${\bb H}^2$ by congruent $n$-gons, such that all vertices have degree 3 and the vertex sets satisfy certain balance condition. For the special case $n=7$, we show that the heptagon in any such tiling belongs to one of the four families, and tilings of ${\bb H}^2$ by generic heptagons in each family is unique. As a consequence, for any closed hyperbolic surface of Euler characteristic $χ$, we may classify all tilings of the surface by maximal number $-6χ$ of congruent generic heptagons in the four families.

title: Snowflake $q$-Flipping
summary: We prove a weighted extension of Byun's snowflake-flipping theorem for cored hexagons with unit triangular holes along three crossing lines. The ratio of the tiling generating functions of two regions related by a snowflake flip is given by an explicit product. The result recovers Byun's theorem when all lozenge weights are 1 and resolves an open problem posed by the author in 2024. Our proof uses shuffling identities for semihexagons with dents on two sides.

title: The strong cylinder conjecture and Rédei's factorization conjecture in three dimensions
summary: In this paper, we prove the strong cylinder conjecture, that is, for every prime $p$, a set of $p^2$ points in $\mathbb F_p^3$ that meets every affine plane in a multiple of $p$ points is a union of $p$ distinct parallel affine lines. We use this result to resolve Rédei's 1970 factorization conjecture in three dimensions: if $A,B\subseteq\mathbb F_p^3$ contain zero and every vector in $\mathbb F_p^3$ has a unique expression $a+b$ with $a\in A$ and $b\in B$, then one of the two sets is contained in a plane through zero.

title: Multiparameter counting of numerical semigroups by Frobenius number, genus, and multiplicity
summary: A numerical semigroup is a subset of the nonnegative integers, closed under addition and with finite complement. The size of the complement is its genus. The problem of counting semigroups by the largest gap got very important through the so-called Frobenius problem, first documented in 1884. Accordingly, the largest gap is called the Frobenius number. In the last two decades, counting by the genus has become a subject of even more intense study, mostly because of the non-solved conjectures on its monotonic and super-Fibonacci growth. It is known that the number of semigroups of each genus grows asymptotically with the genus like the Fibonacci numbers and that the number of semigroups of each Frobenius number grows asymptotically in such a way that each number doubles the previous but one. We prove a formula for the number of numerical semigroups of each Frobenius number, genus, and multiplicity (first nonzero nongap), under the assumption that the multiplicity $m$ and the Frobenius number $F$ satisfy $m\geq\frac{F+1}{3}$. It has been proved that asymptotically almost all semigroups satisfy this condition. From this formula we prove multiparameter recurrence relations. They give, under the required restriction, a multiparameter exact version of the increasing behaviours previously mentioned. Indeed, we prove that the number $n_{F,m,g}$ of semigroups with Frobenius number $F$, multiplicity $m$ and genus $g$ satisfies $n_{F,m,g}=n_{F-2,m-1,g-1}+n_{F-2,m-1,g-2}$ and that the number $n_{F,m}$ of semigroups with Frobenius number $F$ and multiplicity $m$ satisfies $n_{F,m}=2n_{F-2,m-1}.$

title: Kronecker coefficients of large degree and Littlewood-Richardson inequalities
summary: We prove that Kronecker coefficients are uniformly asymptotic to $f^λf^μf^ν/n!$ when all three irreducible dimensions are at least $\sqrt{n!}\,e^{-A\sqrt n}$, for any fixed $A>0$. This strengthens a conjecture of Pak, Panova and Yeliussizov. For triple staircase and triple square partitions, we obtain relative asymptotics with respective limiting factors $e^{-1/24}$ and $e^{-1/3}$. For Littlewood-Richardson (LR) coefficients, we bound the sum of the three dimension deficits by the LR coefficient deficit times $O(\log n)$, proving their Conjecture 5.5 and extending it to arbitrary fixed size proportions. We also construct vanishing LR coefficients with three Plancherel dimension sequences and determine the exact stabilization threshold of the largest LR coefficient with one input size fixed.

title: When Strategies Do Not Determine Play: Infinite Hat-Guessing Games on Subsets of the Reals
summary: We study infinite hat-guessing games indexed by linearly ordered sets $S\subseteq\mathbb R$, where players guess sequentially using information determined by the order. While well-ordered standing sets admit the naive, recursive definition of play, we found a surprising example showing that this approach fails for non-well-ordered ones, where local decision rules do not determine a unique global outcome. By requiring uniqueness of play, we aim to provide a natural framework for hat-guessing games on arbitrary standing sets. For the classical visibility model, it was previously known due to Glivický that at most one incorrect guess can be guaranteed when $S$ is well-ordered. We prove the same result for backwards well-ordered sets, even in the case when $S$ has no first element. In the full-visibility version of the game, Glivický proved that at most one incorrect guess can be guaranteed if the standing set has a first element. We extend this result to arbitrary nonempty standing sets.

title: Combinatorial Invariants for Metacyclic Groups
summary: We study product-one invariants of finite metacyclic groups, with particular attention to metacyclic $p$-groups. For semidirect products $C_n\rtimes C_m$ such that $\operatorname{ord}_n(\ell)=m$ and $\operatorname{ord}_q(\ell)=m$ for every prime divisor $q$ of $n$, we give a short proof of the known formula for the small Davenport constant and determine the exact value of the $η$-constant. When $n=p$ is prime, we use Vosper's theorem to obtain a growth result for products of non-trivial conjugacy classes contained in $C_p$, from which we derive a block-saturation principle for product-one sequences. For split metacyclic $p$-groups, we determine the small Davenport constant in terms of the order and the exponent, and obtain bounds for the $η$-constant and the Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv constant. The Davenport bound is also extended to finite nilpotent split metacyclic groups. Our approach relies in part on a general quotient-lifting principle for the three invariants $\mathsf d$, $η$, and $\mathsf s$. For non-cyclic metacyclic $p$-groups, this principle applies through the Frattini quotient, which is isomorphic to $C_p^2$. We further establish upper and lower bounds for the Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv constant of arbitrary metacyclic $p$-groups, and show that both bounds are best possible within this class. The lifting method also provides a short proof of a known theorem of Han and Zhang for groups $C_m\ltimes C_n$ with $m\mid n$. Finally, we determine the Olson constant of the dihedral group $D_{2p}$, for every prime $p>3$, in terms of the Olson constant of $C_p$.

title: Homomesy of tropical $T$-systems for pairs of simply laced Dynkin diagrams
summary: For a pair of simply laced Dynking diagrams $X$ and $X'$, we prove Chin's homomesy conjecture on the number of red and blue mutations in a period of the tropical Zamolodchikov $T$-system associated to $(X, X')$ using Nakanishi's dilogarithm identity.

title: The minimum forcing number of graphs and involutory weighted adjacency matrices
summary: Let $G$ be a graph with a perfect matching. The minimum forcing number $f(G)$ of $G$ is the smallest size of a matching in $G$ that is contained in exactly one perfect matching. For the $d$-hypercube $Q_d$ ($d\geq 2$) Diwan (2019) determined $f(Q_d)=2^{d-2}$ by using a linear algebraic method, and Mohammadian (2022) generalized this method and showed that $f(G\square K_2)=n/2$ when a bipartite graph $G$ admits order $n$ and an involutory weighted adjacency matrix over a field $\mathbb F$, where $\square$ denotes the Cartesian product. In this paper, we further prove that if $\operatorname{char}\mathbb{F}\neq 2$, then $\frac{n}{2}\le f(G\mathbin{\square} P_k)\le \frac{n}{2}\lceil\frac{k}{2}\rceil$ for every $k\ge 2$, where $P_k$ is the $k$-vertex path; this recovers Mohammadian's result when $k=2$, and the lower bound is attained for $k=3$. Moreover, we extend this method to non-bipartite graphs. Recursively constructing the adjacency matrix of the folded hypercube $FQ_n$ over the binary field $\mathbb F_2$, we prove that $f(FQ_n\mathbin{\square} K_2)=2^{n-1}$ for every even $n$. Combined with Mohammadian's result for odd $n$, this establishes the same formula for all $n\geq 1$.

title: A Cameron-Goethals-Seidel-Shult theorem for marked graphs
summary: The classical Cameron-Goethals-Seidel-Shult theorem characterizes graphs with least eigenvalue at least $-2$ in terms of generalized line graphs, exceptional graphs, and root systems. In this paper, we establish a marked graph extension of this theorem. For a graph $G$ on $n$ vertices and a binary vector $\mathbf{b}\in\{0,1\}^n$, we completely characterize all marked graphs $\mathbf{G}=(G,\mathbf{b})$ such that $λ_{\min}(A(G)+\mathbf{b}\mathbf{b}^\top-J_n)\ge -2$, where $J_n$ denotes the all-ones matrix of order $n$. Using representations by finite root systems, we show that every irreducible marked graph satisfying the above inequality is represented by either the root system $B_n$ or the exceptional root system $E_8$. This leads to a complete structural characterization in terms of irreducible marked graphs, namely induced subgraphs of extended generalized line graphs, the marked graph $(2K_1,\mathbf{0})$, and exceptional graphs with all vertices marked. In the special case $\mathbf{b}=\mathbf{j}$, our characterization reduces to the original Cameron-Goethals-Seidel-Shult theorem. The root system $B_n$ and extended generalized line graphs play the roles occupied by $D_n$ and generalized line graphs in the classical theory. We further apply the characterization to graphs whose second largest eigenvalue is at most $1$, showing that every $-2$-markable graph satisfies this spectral condition.

title: Five-Entropic Matroids Are Quinary
summary: A finite matroid is representable over a field if its elements can be assigned vectors over that field such that the rank of every subset equals the dimension of the span of its vectors. For an integer q >= 2, a matroid is q-entropic if there exists a random vector indexed by its ground set, with each coordinate taking values in a common q-element alphabet, such that the entropy of every marginal subvector equals the rank of the corresponding subset multiplied by log q. It remains open to determine for which values of q every q-entropic matroid is representable over a field. For q=2 and q=3, representability over F_q has long been known. More recently, it was established that every 4-entropic matroid is representable over F_4 and that the 6-entropic matroids are precisely the regular matroids, that is, those representable over every field. We settle the previously unresolved five-symbol case, proving that a finite matroid is 5-entropic if and only if it is representable over F_5. For the nontrivial implication, we use Matúš's equivalence between entropic and partition representations. We show that a degree-five partition representation induces, on each embedded U_{2,4}-minor, an F_5-linear representation after coordinatewise relabeling, with a rescaling class independent of the chosen linearization. Using the foundation presentation of Baker and Lorscheid, we verify the compatibility relations among these local classes and thereby obtain a global F_5-representation.

title: Spectral conditions for the existence of $\{K_2,\{C_k\}\}$-factor in $t$-tough graphs
summary: For $t>0$, a graph $G$ is called $t$-tough if $|S|\geq t\,c(G-S)$ for every $S\subseteq V(G)$ with $c(G-S)\geq2$, where $c(G-S)$ denotes the number of components of $G-S$. Toughness is closely related to the existence of Hamiltonian cycles and factors in graphs. Chvátal [Discrete Math. 5 (1973) 215--228] conjectured that there exists a constant $t_0>0$ such that every $t_0$-tough graph of order at least three is Hamiltonian. Bauer, Broersma and Veldman [Discrete Appl. Math. 99 (2000) 317--321] constructed $(9/4-\varepsilon)$-tough graphs without a Hamiltonian path for arbitrarily small $\varepsilon>0$. For the weaker requirement of a $2$-factor, Enomoto et al. [J. Graph Theory 9 (1985) 87--95] proved that every $2$-tough graph of order at least three has a $2$-factor and that the toughness threshold $2$ is best possible. A graph $G$ is said to have a $\{K_2,\{C_k:k\geq3\}\}$-factor if and only if $G$ contains a spanning subgraph consisting of components that are either cycles or single edges. A $\{K_2,\{C_k:k\geq3\}\}$-factor can be viewed as a combination of a $1$-factor and a $2$-factor, motivating the study of such factors in tough graphs. In this paper, we establish sharp sufficient conditions in terms of the adjacency spectral radius, the distance spectral radius, and the distance signless Laplacian spectral radius for a $t$-tough graph to have a $\{K_2,\{C_k:k\geq3\}\}$-factor.

title: Equality in the direction bound over prime fields
summary: Let $p$ be prime. We prove that a noncollinear set of $2m+1\le p$ points in $\AG(2,p)$ determines exactly $m+2$ directions if and only if, up to an affine transformation, it consists of the origin and a coset of a multiplicative subgroup of order $m$ on each coordinate axis. Thus equality is possible precisely when $m\mid p-1$. This extends the Lovász--Schrijver classification for $2m+1=p$.

title: Good colorings of doubled triangles and a conjecture of Schwartz
summary: A good coloring of a sphere triangulation is a black-and-white coloring of its faces such that, at every vertex, the numbers of black and white faces differ by a multiple of~$3$. Good colorings correspond to proper vertex $4$-colorings. For a good coloring with fold count $\mathrm{f}$ (the number of black-white edges) on a triangulation with $F$ faces, R.~E.~Schwartz introduced the Eisenstein isoperimetric ratio $η=\mathrm{f}^2/F$. For triangulations with degree sequence $6,\dots,6,2,2,2$, he proved that $η\ge3$ and conjectured that every such triangulation has a good coloring with $η$ below a universal constant. These triangulations are indexed by the nonzero Eisenstein integers~$β$. We study the family $\T(n)$ given by $β=n$, a positive integer, which consists of the doubled equilateral triangles of side~$n$. We prove that every good coloring of $\T(n)$ has at least $3n$ folds, so $η\ge9/2$, and that this bound is attained for every~$n$. Thus the minimum of $η$ on this family is exactly $9/2$, and Schwartz's conjecture holds for it. We also prove that subdividing a good coloring of $\T(β)$ gives a good coloring of $\T(nβ)$ with the same value of $η$. Consequently, Schwartz's conjecture holds in general if and only if it holds for primitive Eisenstein integers.

title: Permutons
summary: Permutons are limit structures for large permutations. Intrinsically, a permuton is a familiar mathematical object: a probability measure on the unit square with uniform marginals. The compact space of permutons completes the set of permutations of all sizes under a natural topology; each permuton is not only a limit of permutations but also a generator of random permutations. Since their (relatively recent) discovery as a tool for understanding the behavior of large (possibly random) permutations, permutons have proved remarkably fruitful, with dozens of fascinating connections to combinatorics and probability. We review the fundamentals of permutons, sometimes providing new, shorter proofs, and give an account of some of their myriad applications. The survey concludes with a long list of open problems. An extensive -- but not comprehensive -- bibliography is appended.

title: The strong cylinder conjecture over prime fields
summary: Let $p$ be prime and let $S\subseteq\mathbb F_p^3$ have $p^2$ points, with every affine plane meeting $S$ in a multiple of $p$ points. We give a self-contained argument that $S$ is a union of $p$ parallel lines.

title: A Rooted Structure Theorem for $5$-Connected Graphs and $K_6^-$-Minors
summary: Jorgensen conjectured that every $6$-connected graph with no $K_6$-minor is apex. For a $6$-connected graph containing a $K_4$ on vertices $a_1,\dots,a_4$, being apex is equivalent to $G-a_i$ having a planar embedding with the other three roots on a common face for some $i$, so that for such graphs the conjecture becomes a rooted planarity statement. Robertson, Seymour, and Thomas showed that the failure of the corresponding three-rooted planarity is witnessed by a legless tripod. We introduce a four-root structure, called a frame, that extends this certificate, and prove a structural theorem: every $5$-connected graph containing a frame rooted at four prescribed vertices contains a subgraph of one of five explicit types, denoted $A$--$E$. This theorem does not depend on the edges among the roots. As an application, we show that when the four roots span a $K_4^-$, each of the five configurations yields a $K_6^-$-minor. Together with a planar argument for the case without a frame and an induction based on a theorem of Kawarabayashi, this gives a proof that every non-planar $5$-connected graph contains a $K_6^-$-minor. This statement also follows from a recent theorem of Lo; our proof is independent and is driven by the rooted structure theorem, whose method we expect to apply to Jorgensen's conjecture with other target configurations.

title: Hilton's Conjecture on Uncomplemented Incomparable Families
summary: A family ${\mathcal A}\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ is \emph{uncomplemented} if it contains no set together with its complement. Families ${\mathcal A}_1,\ldots,{\mathcal A}_t$ are \emph{strongly incomparable} if every set in one family is incomparable with every set in another family. In 1976, Hilton conjectured that if ${\mathcal A}_1,\ldots,{\mathcal A}_t\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ are uncomplemented and strongly incomparable, then $$\sum_{i=1}^t |{\mathcal A}_i|\le 2^{n-1}.$$ We confirm this conjecture by a matrix rank argument that encodes incomparability and uncomplementedness in the same matrix, which is quite different from the earlier methods on this problem. We also study weak incomparability, in which the same set may occur in different families. Goldwasser, Hilton and Zheng conjectured an upper bound in this setting and claimed that their conjecture is equivalent to Hilton's conjecture. We give counterexamples to their conjecture for every $t\ge3$ and identify the error in the claimed equivalence. We then propose a replacement conjecture and confirm it when $t$ is large. The upper bound $2^{n-1}$ in Hilton's conjecture can be attained if some families are allowed to by empty. It is natural to consider the maximum size of $\sum_{i=1}^t |{\mathcal A}_i|$ for uncomplemented and strongly incomparable families ${\mathcal A}_1,\ldots,{\mathcal A}_t\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ when all families are required to be non-empty. Denote this maximum number by $M(n,t)$. We show that \[ 2^{n-1}-1\le M(n,t)\le 2^{n-1} \] for $n\ge3$ and $3\le t\le n$.

title: A criterion for the set of subsums to be a Cantorval for a certain class of multigeometric series
summary: The paper studies the topological structure of the set of subsums (incomplete sums) of multigeometric series of the form $\frac{k_1}{s} + \frac{k_2}{s} + \ldots + \frac{k_m}{s} + \frac{k_1}{s^2} + \frac{k_2}{s^2} + \ldots+ \frac{k_m}{s^2} + \frac{k_1}{s^3} + \frac{k_2}{s^3} +\ldots$, where $k_1, \ldots, k_m, s \in \mathbb{N}$. In terms of graph theory, necessary and sufficient conditions are established for the set of subsums of a given series not to be a finite union of closed intervals, as well as necessary and sufficient conditions for this set to contain an interval. As a consequence of these statements, a criterion for the set of subsums to be a Cantorval is obtained. An example of applying the criterion to a series whose Cantorval property was previously unknown is given. A more general object of study of topological properties is the set of numbers whose representations in a numerical system with a natural base and a redundant alphabet are subject to restrictions on the use of digits. It is for this object that the above statements are proved.

title: Globally Simple Heffter Arrays $H(n;k)$ with $k \equiv 2 \pmod{4}$
summary: Heffter arrays are combinatorial structures that can be used to construct orthogonal cyclic cycle decompositions of complete graphs. A square Heffter array $H(n;k)$ is a partially filled $n \times n$ array with $k$ filled cells in each row and column. Its entries are distinct and nonzero, form a half-set of the group $\mathbb{Z}_{2nk+1}$, and sum to zero in every row and column. If the natural orderings of the rows and columns of an array are simple, the array is called globally simple. The globally simple property guarantees the orthogonal cycle decompositions constructed from the Heffter array consist of simple cycles. While existence results are known for most congruence classes of the parameters $n$ and $k$ modulo 4 for square globally simple Heffter arrays $H(n;k)$, the existence for $k \equiv 2 \pmod{4}$ has remained largely open. In this paper, we present a construction for globally simple integer Heffter arrays $H(n;k)$ covering all admissible values of $n$ when $k \equiv 2 \pmod{4}$. This settles the existence question across all congruence classes.

title: Cube tilings, partition counters, and the Calkin--Wilf and Kepler trees
summary: A tiling of the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ by translates of the discrete cube $K_d=\{0,1\}^d$ cuts every translate $K_d+x$ into subcubes. We study the function $\ell(x)$ counting these parts. Its sum over every translate of $K_d$ equals $3^d$, for an arbitrary translation set. For lattice tilings with a triangular basis we obtain a dimension-reduction formula, and we describe every cocyclic lattice by a single normalized congruence. Along a cyclic generator, the counter of a signed bidiagonal lattice is a row of Stern's diatomic sequence; pairs of counter values realize the Calkin--Wilf tree, and complementary binary words realize the Kepler tree. For the binary lattice, the translated counter labelings of the cube carry generating face partitions, supplied by the tiling itself, which force the levels of the Kepler tree, and every nontrivial face partition has a unique lamination direction. Using finite Fourier analysis we prove that the ordered cyclic profile determines a standard cocyclic cube tiling lattice up to coordinate reflections. For lattices tiling by discrete boxes we determine exactly when the analogous statement holds.

title: Odd realisation numbers of rigid graphs
summary: Determining the number of realisations of a rigid graph for a specific choice of edge lengths is a fundamental problem in discrete geometry. Gortler, Healy and Thurston showed that the number of real realisations of a generic framework is always even or equal to one. Despite being rare, there do exist graphs whose number of complex realisations is odd and not equal to one. In this article, we exhibit two necessary conditions for a rigid graph to have an odd realisation number other than one. We also provide an infinite family of rigid graphs with an odd realisation number other than one.

title: Upper bounds on all-terminal reliability polynomials in terms of cycle basis lengths
summary: Let $G=(V(G),E(G))$ be a connected multigraph with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges. The all-terminal reliability polynomial of $G$ can be written as $R_G(q)=(1-q)^{n-1}\sum\limits_{i=0}^{d}H_iq^i$ where $d=m-n+1$ is the cycle rank, each edge fails independently with probability $q\in[0,1]$, and $H_0,\ldots,H_d$ are the associated coefficients. A cycle basis, which consists of cycles that form a basis of the cycle space of a graph, is an important tool for characterizing its cycle structure. The structural properties of cycle bases, together with the associated length optimization problems and construction algorithms, have been extensively studied. In this context, Colbourn posed the following open problem, which concerns upper bounds on the reliability coefficients in terms of cycle-basis lengths: For all-terminal reliability, is it true that if $G$ has a cycle basis containing cycles of lengths $c_1,\ldots,\allowbreak c_{m-n+1}$, then $H_i \le\sum\limits_{\substack{I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m-n+1\},|I|=i}}\prod\limits_{j\in I}(c_j-1)$? In this paper, we establish a result that resolves this open problem.

title: Piercing a Chessboard with Restricted Slopes
summary: Is it true that for $n\geq 3$, $n-1$ lines are needed to pierce every cell of an $n\times n$ board? This problem was independently rediscovered several times: Alkauskas (1998), Harel-Ackerman-Pinchasi (2012, without claiming the $n-1$ bound), Bárány-Frankl (2021). However, apparently the first to pose it was T. Keller (Honolulu, Hawaii), in 1980, in the problem section of The American Mathematical Monthly. In this note, we give an affirmative answer to Keller's problem when all lines have slopes in $(-\infty,-1]\cup(0,1]$.

title: Cut Conditions, Integrality, and Obstructions for Directed Multiflows
summary: In contrast to the max-flow/min-cut theorem for single-commodity flows, the cut condition is necessary but not sufficient for the existence of directed multiflows, even with only two commodities. Poremba and Shepherd (IPCO 2023) conjecture that the cut condition is sufficient for all capacities and demands on a directed two-commodity topology if and only if it contains neither of two specific topologies as a relevant minor. We prove this conjecture. As a consequence, the fractional and integral flow-cut gaps of every directed two-commodity topology coincide and are either 1 or 2. We then investigate stronger necessary conditions for multiflow feasibility and their implications for integrality. We introduce a hierarchy of five conditions, ranging from the classical cut condition through conditions based on blocking edge sets and binary edge lengths to the linear programming dual characterization of fractional feasibility. The corresponding classes of sufficient topologies are strictly nested. We extend the Nagamochi-Ibaraki theorem: whenever one of the first four conditions is sufficient on a topology, integral capacities and demands satisfying that condition admit an integral multiflow, computable in polynomial time. Finally, we prove that recognizing topologies on which any of these four conditions is sufficient is coNP-complete, even for two commodities.

title: Sufficient conditions for spanning trees with bounded total excess in tough graphs
summary: Let $G$ be a connected graph and $T$ a spanning tree of $G$. The toughness of $G$ is defined by $t(G)=\min\Big\{\frac{|S|}{c(G-S)}:S\subseteq V(G), c(G-S)\geq2\Big\}$ for $G\neq K_n$. A graph $G$ is said to be $t$-tough if $t(G)\geq t$. The size, the adjacency spectral radius and the signless Laplacian spectral radius of $G$ are denoted by $e(G)$, $ρ(G)$ and $q(G)$, respectively. The $k$-excess of a vertex $v$ in $T$ is defined as $\max\{0,d_T(v)-k\}$. The total $k$-excess $\mbox{te}(T,k)$ is defined by $\mbox{te}(T,k)=\sum\limits_{v\in V(T)}{\max\{0,d_T(v)-k\}}$. A tree $T$ is called a $k$-tree if $d_T(v)\leq k$ for every $v\in V(T)$, namely, the maximum degree of a $k$-tree is at most $k$. It is obvious that $T$ is a spanning $k$-tree if and only if $\mbox{te}(T,k)=0$. This paper investigates a generalization of spanning $k$-trees using a concept called total $k$-excess and puts forward three lower bounds based on $e(G)$, $ρ(G)$ and $q(G)$ in a connected $\frac{k}{k(k-2)+b+3}$-tough graph $G$ to guarantee that $G$ has a spanning tree $T$ with $\mbox{te}(T,k)\leq b$, where $k\geq3$ and $b\geq0$ are two integers. As corollaries, we obtain three sufficient conditions for a connected $\frac{k}{k(k-2)+3}$-tough graph to has a spanning $k$-tree.

title: Edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles in the McKay--Miller--Širáň graphs $H_q$ for every prime power $q\geq 3$
summary: Motivated by Hamilton cycle problems and applications to collective communication, we study edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles in the McKay--Miller--Širáň (MMS) graphs. The MMS graph $H_q$ (indexed by a prime power $q$) is a highly symmetric graph arising from finite fields. For every prime power $q\geq 3$, we prove that the MMS graph $H_q$ contains $\big\lceil\frac{q-1}{2}\big\rceil$ edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles. This resolves a problem of Li, Wang and Zheng, who established the result for prime $q$ and for $q=4$. Our construction uses graph lifts over finite fields and joins the components of lifted Hamilton cycles by adding edges within vertex fibres. The resulting cycles can be constructed using $O(|E(H_q)|)$ finite field operations, comparisons, and elementary list operations. As an application, these cycles provide edge-disjoint spanning rings for parallel ring-all-reduce algorithms on MMS networks.

title: Induced packing treewidth III. Branch decompositions
summary: The notion of induced packing treewidth aims to unify classes defined by forbidden induced subgraphs or induced minors with classes defined by the existence of certain structured tree decompositions. In this paper, we introduce induced packing branchwidth, a branch-decomposition analogue of induced packing treewidth. For a graph $H$, the induced $H$-packing branchwidth of a graph $G$, denoted by $\branchpi_H(G)$, is the minimum, over all branch decompositions of $G$, of the largest number of pairwise anticomplete induced copies of $H$ that cross one displayed cut. For $H=P_2$, it equals sim-width. We prove several structural properties of graphs of bounded $\branchpi_H$, for various choices of $H$, including $χ$-boundedness, polynomial degree-boundedness, and metric properties.

title: Avoiding short progressions in Euclidean Ramsey theory II
summary:
Recently, Currier, Moore, and Yip developed a general framework for constructing colorings avoiding prescribed monochromatic arithmetic progressions in Euclidean Ramsey theory. Writing $\ell_m$ for an $m$-term arithmetic progression with unit spacing, they proved $\mathbb E^n
ot	o(\ell_3,\ell_{20})$ and $\mathbb E^n
ot	o(\ell_3,α\ell_{6889})$ for every $α>0$. We refine and simplify their framework, proving $\mathbb E^n
ot	o(\ell_3,α\ell_{22})$ for every $α>0$. We further establish $\mathbb E^n
ot	o(\ell_3,α\ell_{21})$ except possibly for four values of $α^2$, and $\mathbb E^n
ot	o(\ell_3,α\ell_{17})$ for all but finitely many $α>0$. Our approach also recovers several earlier results and avoids some technical arguments used in previous works.

title: Sampling Colorings on $G(n, d/n)$ via Glauber Dynamics
summary: We study the mixing time of Glauber dynamics for sampling uniformly from the proper $q$-colorings of sparse Erdős-Rényi random graphs $G(n,d/n)$. Our main result establishes that with probability $1-o(1)$ over the draw of $G$, Glauber dynamics is rapidly mixing for every $q\geq d+d^{1/2+\varepsilon}$, given any fixed $0<\varepsilon\leq1/2$ and any sufficiently large fixed $d$. In particular, the surplus of colors above $d$ is sublinear and close to $\sqrt{d}$. The achieved color range therefore approaches the tree uniqueness threshold and improves over the previously best achievable number of colors $q > 1.763 d$ due to Efthymiou, Hayes, Stefankovic, and Vigoda [SODA 2018]. Moreover, our mixing-time bound is $O(n^{2+o_d(1)})$, and hence almost quadratic as $d\rightarrow\infty$. Our proof is based on establishing a spectral gap for block dynamics resulting from a suitable decomposition of $G(n,d/n)$ into blocks and singleton vertices, ensuring that every high-degree vertex is encapsulated within a block. Our main technical contribution is a novel way of establishing rapid mixing of block dynamics via an integrated Bochner-Bakry-Émery approach, which we expect to have applications beyond sampling colorings. We further devise a new block decomposition of $G(n,d/n)$ that strengthens and simplifies similar constructions used in previous work. Finally, to compare block and Glauber dynamics, we establish a novel recursive separator decomposition of tree-like blocks, together with a coupling argument that avoids the need for nearly uniform color marginals at vertices adjacent to hubs. This comparison argument might be of independent interest.

title: A proof of the Theta conjecture
summary: We prove the touching refinement of the Theta conjecture of Interdonato and Iraci, giving a formula for $Θ_{e_\ell}Θ_{e_k}\nabla E_{d,j}$ as a weighted sum over parking functions with decorated rises and valleys and touch number $j$. Summing over $j$ gives the Theta conjecture. As corollaries, we prove the valley Delta conjecture of Haglund, Remmel, and Wilson and its generalized version proposed by Qiu and Wilson. Our proof compares algebraic and combinatorial recurrences using an extension of the plethystic substitution $X\mapsto(q-1)X$ to quasisymmetric functions. The algebraic recurrence follows from an endomorphism constructed by D'Adderio, Interdonato, Iraci and Pagaria on the Dyck path algebra of Carlsson and Mellit. The combinatorial recurrence is obtained by introducing signed labels and deleting the main diagonal. The two recurrences have the same initial conditions, which identifies the corresponding generating functions.

title: Exact local spectral thresholds for loose and tight Hamilton cycles in $3$-graphs
summary: For an $n$-vertex $3$-uniform hypergraph $H$, let $σ(H)$ denote the minimum adjacency spectral radius of its vertex links. We determine the exact thresholds for $σ(H)$ that force loose and tight Hamilton cycles for all sufficiently large admissible orders, and give constructions showing that each bound is best possible. The loose threshold is $(1+\sqrt{13})n/8+O(1)$, with two forms according to $n$ modulo four. The tight threshold is $2n/3+O(1)$, with four forms determined by $n$ modulo three and, when $3\mid n$, modulo nine. The resulting spectral conditions and the corresponding minimum vertex degree conditions do not imply one another. For loose cycles, we combine fractional packing stability and absorption with exact completion near a space barrier. For tight cycles, spectral stability and rooted sampling reduce the problem to three extremal configurations. We resolve these configurations by controlling the spectral loss caused by missing triples and constructing short paths that extend to Hamilton cycles, including in the presence of exceptional vertices.

title: Chvátal's Toughness Conjecture for Dense Almost Regular Graphs
summary: Chvátal's toughness conjecture asserts that there is a constant $t_0$ such that every $t_0$-tough graph on at least three vertices is Hamiltonian. Most partial results on this conjecture concern graphs with a restricted structure, such as chordal graphs and $H$-free graphs for small linear forests $H$. We confirm the conjecture with $t_0=4$ for dense almost regular graphs, without any structural assumption: for every $α>0$, there exist $\varepsilon>0$ and $n_0$ such that every $4$-tough graph $G$ on $n\ge n_0$ vertices with $δ(G)\geαn$ and $Δ(G)-δ(G)\le\varepsilon n$ is Hamiltonian. This result also bears on a conjecture of Bollobás and, independently, Häggkvist from the 1970s that every $k$-connected $D$-regular graph on $n$ vertices with $D\ge n/(k+1)$ is Hamiltonian. This conjecture is false for every $k\ge4$, even for large $n$. Our result shows that its conclusion holds for all large $n$ when $k$-connectivity is replaced by $4$-toughness, and that the degree condition can then be weakened to $D\geαn$ for an arbitrarily small fixed $α>0$. We also construct $3/2$-tough regular non-Hamiltonian graphs of linear degree, showing that the constant $4$ cannot be replaced by $3/2$.

title: Exact codegree Turán densities of even zycles
summary: We determine the exact codegree Turán density of the $3$-uniform zycle $Z_\ell$ for every even integer $\ell\ge 8$ with $3\nmid\ell$,showing that $γ(Z_\ell)=1/3$. More generally, we prove that $γ(Z_\ell)\le 1/3$ for all even $\ell\ge 8$. Our results partially answer a question of Piga and Schülke [Bull. Lond. Math. Soc. 58 (2026), e70348] concerning the sharpness of their upper bound of $1/2$.

title: Permutation symmetries and characteristic polynomials
summary: We compute certain multilinear functionals of permutation-invariant random matrices, following the work of Marcus and Geneson. As an application, we derive formulae for the average characteristic polynomial of the sum and the product of permutation-invariant random matrices.

title: Budan--Fourier theorem for circuit polynomial systems
summary: We prove a Budan--Fourier theorem for linear combinations of analytic functions whose successive Wronskians are positive: the number of zeros of $g=\sum_{k=1}^s c_kh_k$ in an interval $(a,b]$, counted with multiplicities, is bounded by the drop of the number of sign changes of the sequence of Wronskians $W(h_1,\ldots,h_{k-1},g)$ between $a$ and $b$, and the difference is even. This refines the bound $s-1$ of Koiran, Portier and Tavenas, and we show that it applies, after a suitable renumbering, to any sequence of functions satisfying Descartes' rule of signs. We then study the functions arising from polynomial systems supported on circuits, that is, systems of $n$ equations in $n$ variables with $n+2$ monomials. For these functions, we show that the Budan--Fourier bound never exceeds Descartes' bound, and we compute it at the endpoints of the interval of definition. As an application, we obtain a refinement of the optimal Descartes' rule of signs for circuits of Bihan, Dickenstein and Forsgård: we bound the number of positive solutions whose logarithm lies in explicit polytopes, these bounds add up to at most the bound of Bihan, Dickenstein and Forsgård, and they determine the parity of the number of positive solutions.

title: On Symmetric Chain Decompositions for Bruhat--Chevalley Posets
summary: We consider Stanley's problem on describing symmetric chain decompositions for the Bruhat--Chevalley posets of partial flag varieties and, more generally, Schubert varieties. These posets describe the containment relations of cell closures in the partial flag variety $G/P$ of a connected complex reductive algebraic group $G$. A famous instance of this problem asks whether the poset of partitions that fit inside a rectangle ordered by containment admits a symmetric chain decomposition (SCD), corresponding to the case of Grassmannian Schubert varieties in type $A$. Our first main result applies the ``complete BP decomposition" of Richmond--Slofstra to show that the SCD problem for any rationally smooth Schubert variety reduces to the (generalized) Grassmannian case, in any semisimple type. We further study the SCDs provided by codes for Bruhat--Chevalley posets in type $A$. These SCDs can be viewed as a consequence of a particular form of complete BP decomposition. In particular, we show that a poset of permutation-labeled partitions in a rectangle corresponding to the quotient $\mathcal{S}_n/\mathcal{S}_{n-k}$ admits an SCD. Further, posets of weak compositions inside a rectangle are realized as Bruhat--Chevalley intervals with associated codes and SCDs.

title: The dimension of multi-index assignment polytopes and Latin-square transversal polytopes, via association schemes
summary: We determine the dimensions, and the implicit equations, of several polytopes from integer programming whose vertices are the largest stable sets of highly symmetric graphs. Our main tools are two new dimension formulae within Lee's spectral method, which reads the dimension off of an association scheme: for amorphic schemes it becomes a threshold formula, and for point sets in $GF(q)^d$ invariant under the maps $z\mapsto az+b$ it is $q-1$ times the number of hyperplane directions along which some point is not equidistributed. A single integer point, a witness, then certifies a whole eigenspace. For the multi-index assignment polytopes of Appa, Magos, and Mourtos at prime-power orders, the dimension equals that of the linear relaxation except in two infinite families, which are, to our knowledge, the first counterexamples to their expectation that the two always coincide. The missing equations are explicit clique equations that the standard integer-programming formulation omits. For every abelian group with a transversal, the Latin-square transversal polytope of its Cayley table, equivalently the polytope of rainbow perfect matchings of the corresponding edge-colored $K_{n,n}$ , has the maximal dimension ${(n-1)(n-2)}$; the witnesses come from new constructions of complete mappings. We also treat transversals of Desarguesian nets and the largest sets of symmetric $3\times3$ and $4\times4$ matrices over $GF(q)$ whose differences have rank at least $3$, of sizes $q^3$ and $q^5$.

title: Average distance and maximum induced linear forest
summary: Let G be a connected graph of order n, let μ(G) denote its average distance, and let L(G) denote the maximum order of an induced linear forest of G, that is, of an induced subgraph whose components are chains. Hansen, Hertz, Kilani, Marcotte and Schindl conjectured that μ(G) {\le} L(G)/2, which can be written as 4W(G) {\le} L(G)n(n-1), where W(G) is the Wiener index of G. This inequality strengthens their bound μ(G) {\le} F(G)/2, where F(G) is the maximum order of an induced forest, as well as Chung's classical bound μ(G) {\le} α(G). In this paper we prove the conjecture for all connected graphs.
