title: Permutations, Pattern Covers, Posets and Positivity, Part II: Regular Pattern Packings and Moment Sequences
summary: We prove that broad families of regular pattern packings are enumerated by moments of probability measures on $[0,\infty)$. A packing prescribes occurrences of a consecutive permutation pattern at equally spaced positions, with successive occurrences overlapping and together covering the permutation. This regularity underlies the structure theory for the associated pattern-packing posets that we developed in Part I (arXiv:2610.29846). We obtain moment representations for all two-level shifted-grid families of Part I and all overlap-one patterns whose first and last letters differ by one or two. For families whose posets are trees with a unique minimum or maximum and overlap at most half the pattern length, positivity instead holds after finitely many initial terms of the enumerating sequence have been discarded. Our proofs develop further enumeration formulas and combine probabilistic constructions with total nonnegativity and weighted paths, yielding explicit laws or continued fractions in several cases. Although a previously conjectured universal moment property fails, our results establish positivity for all packing sequences associated with patterns of length at most four and all but one of the distinct sequences arising from patterns of length five. Extensive numerical evidence suggests that the remaining sequence is also a moment sequence. These results lead us to formulate refined conjectures for all overlap-one patterns and for the shifted-grid families of Part I with arbitrarily many levels.

title: A recursion relation for the coefficients of Swinnerton-Dyer type polynomials
summary: We study a family of polynomials that are very closely related to the Swinnerton-Dyer polynomials. As main result, we determine a recursion relation for the coefficients of this family of polynomials. We briefly explain our own and others' interest in this family of polynomials.

title: A singular homeomorphism between Pierce expansions and continued fraction expansions
summary: In this paper, we study the map $Θ$ which sends each $x\in[0,1]$ to the number whose continued fraction digits are the first Pierce expansion digit of $x$ and the gaps between two consecutive Pierce expansion digits of $x$. We investigate the regularity of $Θ$ and $Θ^{-1}$, including the optimal Hölder exponent of $Θ^{-1}$, and the local and Hausdorff dimensions of the push-forwards of the Lebesgue measure under $Θ$ and $Θ^{-1}$. We also study the differentiability of $Θ$ at rational and irrational points, and calculate the Hausdorff dimension of the set of points at which $Θ$ has an infinite derivative.

title: An elliptic deformation of continued fractions
summary: We construct an elliptic deformation $\mathcal{Q}_{a,b;q,p}(x)$ of positive rational numbers $x$ by attaching Schlosser's small elliptic weights $w_{a,b;q,p}(s,t)$ to prefixes of Stern--Brocot words. On positive integers $n$ it gives Schlosser's elliptic numbers $[n]_{a,b;q,p}$. Parameter shifts realize $x \mapsto x+1$ and $x \mapsto x/(x+1)$, while a reciprocal parameter transformation gives an inversion formula. The Gaussian degeneration recovers the $q$-deformed rationals of Morier-Genoud and Ovsienko. The regular and negative elliptic continued fractions agree, since they evaluate the same word with the same ordered weights. The numerator and denominator satisfy weighted Farey recursions and, for rationals greater than $1$, are the closure polynomials, or quiver $F$-polynomials, of the associated oriented type-$A$ quivers. Finally, we express the vertex weights as normalized elliptic Euler expressions of balanced virtual torus representations.

title: Motivic generating functions and $L$-derivatives of cohomological automorphic representations
summary: Forty years ago, Gross and Zagier proved a remarkable formula computing the central derivative of the Rankin--Selberg $L$-function of a cusp form $f$ of weight $2$ and a character of the class group of an imaginary quadratic field, satisfying the so-called Heegner condition, and deduce that the nonvanishing of the central derivative implies the nonvanishing of the corresponding Mordell--Weil rank. This formula was later generalized in various contexts and degrees, for example, by S. Zhang for $f$ of higher even weights; and by Yuan--Zhang--Zhang for $f$ a Hilbert cusp form of parallel weight $2$ over an arbitrary totally real field $F$ and $χ$ a Dirichlet character of an arbitrary CM extension $E/F$, allowing arbitrary ramification. In this article, we prove a Gross--Zagier type formula in the context of doubling method, for $f$ a Hilbert cusp form over $F$ and $χ$ a Hecke character of $E$ of general weights under a balancing condition, again allowing arbitrary ramification. Indeed, we even formulate a general conjecture which we call the motivic arithmetic inner product formula, for cohomological automorphic representations of $\mathrm{GL}_{2r}$ over $E$ of hermitian type of balanced weights.

title: Local vanishing density of order $1$ and Divisor moments
summary: We establish a general framework relating local vanishing densities of order $1$ to logarithmic growth of divisor moments on regular arithmetic curves. As applications, we recover classical divisor moment estimates for polynomial values and establish their function field analogue. Furthermore, under GRH, we obtain a result on divisor moments for polynomials in the Fourier coefficients of non-CM cuspidal eigenforms with trivial nebentypus and trivial inner twist. The Fourier coefficients need not be integers, and the polynomials need not be squarefree. Under additional analytic hypotheses, we also allow a Sato--Tate angle restriction.

title: Multivariate Pellarin $L$-values on algebraic curves
summary: We establish a generating trace formula for multicharacter ideal-type $L$-values associated with rank-one Drinfeld modules. For a sign-normalized Hayes module with free period lattice, the formula realizes the $L$-values at weights $n\equiv s\pmod{q^{°_\infty}-1}$ as a trace over the ordinary Hilbert class field. We further characterize the polynomials in the exponential variable $X$ arising in multicharacter lattice generating identities over arbitrary function rings. Their coefficients are given explicitly via the shtuka basis, which gives concrete control over their supports and degrees. This completely settles an open problem of Pellarin and Perkins: these polynomials are all constant if and only if $s<2q$. The results on coefficients apply to curves of arbitrary genus, infinite places of arbitrary degree, and nonprincipal period lattices.

title: A Goldbach-Type Problem for the Unitary Möbius Function
summary: Let $g(n)=(-1)^{ω(n)}$, where $ω(n)$ denotes the number of distinct prime factors of $n$. We prove that, for every sufficiently large integer $N$, each ordered additive sign pattern $(g(a),g(N-a))=(s,t)$ occurs at least $N/(128(\log N)^3)$ times. We also prove that, for every $N\ge18$ and every $s,t\in\sgnset$, there is at least one integer $1\le a<N$ such that $(g(a),g(N-a))=(s,t)$. In addition, we establish a one-quarter asymptotic formula for almost all target integers. Finally, we discuss Goldbach-type problems for the ordinary Möbius function and formulate related questions.

title: On the error term in Gauss's mean value formulas for class numbers
summary: Combining the frameworks of Chamizo--Iwaniec and Chamizo--Ubis with the recent character-sum and exponential-sum estimates of Bellotti and Kerr, we improve the error term in Gauss's mean value formulas for class numbers of binary quadratic forms from $O(N^{21/32+\eps})$ to $O(N^{55/84+\eps})$. If no Dirichlet $L$-function vanishes in $\mathrm{Re}\,s>7/8$, the exponent becomes $2274811/3487744$; under the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for quadratic Dirichlet $L$-functions, it becomes $118/181$.

title: Trivial solutions in Generalized Fermat equations
summary: The modular method is a powerful tool to study generalized Fermat equations. Trivial solutions often become an obstruction to the method. While using hypergeometric motives to construct Galois representations, some of these solutions give rise to newforms with complex multiplication. In the present article, assuming a standard conjecture in Darmon's program, we prove that asymptotically any newform with complex multiplication cannot be related to a non-trivial primitive solution. This allows to discard all such newforms, including those associated to trivial solutions.

title: Restricted Quantum unique ergodicity under Generalized Lindelöf conjecture
summary: Assume the generalized Lindelöf hypothesis. Let $u$ be an even Hecke--Maass cusp form on $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})\backslash\mathbb{H}$, normalized in $L^2$ with respect to hyperbolic area, with Laplace eigenvalue $1/4+T^2$. For every fixed $ψ\in C_c((0,\infty);\mathbb{C})$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, we prove that \[ \int_0^\infty ψ(y)|u(i y)|^2\frac{d y}{y} =\frac{6}π\int_0^\infty ψ(y)\frac{d y}{y} +O_{ψ,\varepsilon}(T^{-1/4+\varepsilon}) \] as $T\to\infty$, uniformly in $u$. In particular, the restriction mass equidistributes on every fixed compact segment of the imaginary axis in $\mathbb{H}$.

title: A quantitative two-interval criterion for the Riemann hypothesis
summary: We aim to study whether the Weil form can detect a zero of the Riemann zeta function away from the critical line using two functions with increasingly narrow, widely separated supports. We prove that the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality on every such pair at all sufficiently large separations, provided the component widths decrease subexponentially. A zero to the right of the critical line forces the normalized cross term to exceed an exponential at arbitrarily large separations, with any exponent smaller than the horizontal displacement of that zero. In particular, reciprocal-width intervals suffice. Our proof combines a short-support positivity estimate, a smooth partition of fixed test functions and a pole obstruction for a one-sided Laplace transform. We also express the cross term through prime powers in a moving multiplicative interval. The resulting criterion specifies a uniform arithmetic inequality whose proof would establish the Riemann hypothesis.

title: On the lower bound for the $L^1$ norm of Liouville exponential sums. II
summary: Let $λ$ denote the Liouville function, and put \[ I_λ(X)=\int_0^1\left|\sum_{n\le X}λ(n)e^{2πi nα}\right|\,dα. \] In this paper, we prove that \[ \limsup_{X \to \infty} \frac{\log I_λ(X)}{\log X} \ge \frac{1}{3}. \]

title: New lower bounds for even and odd values of the partition function
summary: Let $N_{\mathrm{odd}}(X)$ and $N_{\mathrm{even}}(X)$ denote the numbers of integers $0\leq n< X$ for which the ordinary partition function $p(n)$ is odd and even, respectively. The Parkin--Shanks conjecture predicts that $N_{\mathrm{odd}}(X)$ and $N_{\mathrm{even}}(X)$ are both asymptotic to $X/2$. Bellaïche and Nicolas proved that $N_{\mathrm{even}}(X)\gg \sqrt{X} \log \log X$, while Zheng, building on work of Ono and Swaminathan, recently proved that $N_{\mathrm{odd}}(X)\gg \sqrt{X}$. We improve both bounds simultaneously by proving $\min\{N_{\mathrm{odd}}(X), N_{\mathrm{even}}(X)\}\gg X^{3/4}/(\log X \log \log X)$.

title: Diophantine definitions of nonsplitting for central simple algebras over global fields
summary: For every global field and every fixed degree, we prove that the structure constants defining nonsplit central simple algebras form a diophantine set. We formulate a local witness principle separating reliable localization, exact localization, and local detection. Adapted Kummer and Artin--Schreier presentations provide a common construction of witnesses through a uniform radical formula and ramification matching. This gives an independent proof of the non-characteristic case, which also follows from Morrison's nonnorm theorem, and treats the characteristic-degree case by the same method. We recover prime-degree nonnorm definability and give applications to rootless polynomials, anisotropic quadratic forms in all characteristics, and generalized Severi--Brauer varieties.

title: On mod p Hecke algebras of abstract p-adic automorphic forms
summary: We study completed local shallow Hecke algebras acting on residual automorphic forms attached to projective augmented modules for $\GL_2(\Q_p)$. For odd primes $p$, we prove that the maximal ideal has nilpotence exponent $O(p^{r/2})$ on the level-$r$ generalized eigenspace. For $p\ge5$, if the corresponding Hecke eigenspace in the residual smooth dual has finite length as a $\GL_2(\Q_p)$-representation, then the completed local algebra is noetherian of Krull dimension at least two. If, in addition, its cotangent space has dimension at most two, then it is a formal power series ring in two variables. The nilpotence bound follows by conjugating level subgroups. To deduce the dimension bound, we replace the Fourier pairing in the classical nilpotence method with an inequality comparing the dimension of each finite-level generalized eigenspace with that of its Hecke eigenspace. We apply these results to modular curves and definite quaternion algebras.

title: On Rankin Invariants of Ideal Lattices
summary: The Rankin constant $γ_{n,k}$ measures the largest discriminant of a densest rank $k$ sublattice of a lattice in $\R^n$ over all such lattices of rank $n$ and their exact values are mostly open. For a general lattice $L\subset \R^n$ of rank $n$, the problem of determining its Rankin invariant $γ_{n,k}(L)$ is to find the discriminant of such a densest sublattice. There are no general formulas to compute the discriminant of any arbitrary rank $k$ sublattice. This paper specializes to the case of ideal lattices arising from ideals of number fields, and provides two approaches to study Rankin constants: first, we propose a systematic approach to approximate the minimum discriminant by introducing subideal lattices and proving a closed-form formula to compute $γ^{ideal}_{n,k}(L)$, the ideal Rankin invariant of the ideal lattice. Subsequently, we establish necessary conditions on the underlying number field for the existence of an ideal lattice admitting an optimal subideal lattice with a prescribed minimum discriminant. Secondly, we consider ideal lattices with arbitrary sublattices. We compute $γ_{9,2}$ and improve the current known bounds of the Rankin constants $γ_{5,2}$, $γ_{7,2}$ and $γ_{9,3},γ_{9,4}$, and provide an algebraic construction of the lattice that was used in dimensions $5$ and $7$.

title: Statistics of centralizers of integer matrices
summary: With recent interests on the statistics of commuting integer matrices, we study the related problem on the statistics of the set of centralizer of a matrix. We provide asymptotics and bounds on the size of such set when restricted to integer matrices of bounded height.

title: New families of maximal curves not covered by the Hermitian curve and their cyclic automorphism groups
summary: For every prime power $q>2$, integer $n\ge2$ and $1\le r\le 2n-1$, we construct an $\mathbb F_{q^{2n}}$-maximal curve $T_{q,n,r}$ with Kummer equation \[ z^{q^n+1}=η^{-R}y(1-y^{q-1})^R, \qquad \frac{q^r-1}{q-1},\] where $η\in\mathbb F_{q^{2n}}^*$ satisfies $η^{q^n}=-η$. For fixed $q,n$, these are cyclic covers of the projective line over a single field, indexed by the integer $r$. Writing $δ=\gcd(q^n+1,R)$, we prove that the genus is $(q-1)(q^n+1-δ)/2$ and that $T_{q,n,r}$ is covered by the Hermitian curve $\mathcal H_{q^n}$ over an algebraic closure if and only if $\min(r,2n-r)$ divides $n$. For $1<r<n$ and $δ=1$, the full automorphism group is cyclic of order $(q-1)(q^n+1)$, and distinct values of $r$ give curves that are nonisomorphic over an algebraic closure despite having the same genus and full automorphism group. We also give explicit equations and genera for all their Galois subfields. When $n\ge 4$ is a power of two, this produces families over a fixed field whose members are not covered by $\mathcal H_{q^n}$.

title: On quantitative aspects of ideal membership certificate and GCD inequality for polynomials evaluated at almost units
summary: In this paper, we obtain an effective bounds for the ideal membership certificate in polynomial rings over almost all rings of S-integers, thereby generalizing results of Aschenbrenner and Evertse and Gyory. We also establish an effective refinement of a result of Xiao, building on earlier work of Levin and Corvaja and Zannier. In particular, we provide explicit bounds for both the number and the total degrees of the exceptional hypersurfaces arising in an inequality that bounds the greatest common divisor of multivariable polynomials evaluated at almost S-units under consideration. As an application of our results, we obtain an effective refinement of a theorem of Corvaja and Zannier: Let $(F_n)_n$ and $(G_n)_n$ be two linear recurrence sequences and $\mathcal{N}$ be the set of positive integers $n$ such that $F_n/G_n$ is an integer. Hadamard quotient theorem, conjectured by Pisot and proven by Van der Poorten states that if the set $\mathcal{N}$ coincides with $\mathbb{N}$ then $\left(F_n/G_n\right)_n$ is itself linear recurrence sequence. Corvaja-Zannier proved that if $\mathcal{N}$ is infinite set, then there exists a nonzero polynomial $P(X)$ such that $\left( P(n)F_n/G_n\right)_n$ agrees with a linear recurrence sequence for all $n$ in a suitable arithmetic progression. We give an explicit bound $C$, depending explicitly on the parameters of the recurrence sequences such that, the conclusion holds if $\mathcal{N}$ contains at least $C$ elements.

title: Smooth approximations to character sums and zeta sums
summary: We study smooth approximations to Dirichlet character sums and zeta sums. The uniform upper-bound consequence of the Granville--Soundararajan conjecture, when imposed on all nonprincipal characters including imprimitive ones, implies the Riemann hypothesis for every primitive nonprincipal Dirichlet \(L\)-function. The proof uses characters induced to moduli divisible by all small primes. In the other direction, assuming the Riemann hypothesis for \(L(s,χ)\), we establish the conjectured approximation uniformly for \(q^a\le x\le q\), where \(0<a\le1\) is fixed, with \(y=(\log q+(\log x)^2)(\log\log q)^C\) for every fixed \(C>6\). In this range both the character sum and its smooth restriction, and hence their difference, are exponentially small relative to the number of \(y\)-smooth integers coprime to \(q\). We establish the corresponding approximation for \(\sum_{n\le x}n^{-it}\) under the Riemann hypothesis for the zeta function, uniformly for \(T^a\le x\le T\) and \(2T\le t\le5T\). We also show that the full zeta-sum smooth-approximation conjecture implies the Lindelöf hypothesis.

title: Revisiting the conjectures of Shapiro and Schanuel
summary: We tackle Shapiro's conjecture for exponential polynomials where the coefficients are polynomials, and show that it follows from Schanuel's conjecture. More concretely, given exponential polynomials $f$ and $g$ with infinitely many common zeros, we show that Schanuel's conjecture implies that there is an exponential polynomial $h$ vanishing precisely at all the common zeros of $f$ and $g$.

title: 2-Selmer in arithmetic progressions
summary: We prove uniform asymptotics for the 2-Selmer cardinality in the congruent number family $y^2=x^3-D^2x$ with twisting parameter $D$ restricted to long arithmetic progressions.

title: Monotonicity of Erdős sums
summary: For $k \geq 1$ let $f_k = \sum_{Ω(n)=k} 1/(n\log n)$, where $Ω$ counts prime factors with multiplicity, and let $g_k$ be the same sum restricted to odd $n$. Lichtman showed that $f_k \to 1$, with a global minimum at $k=6$, and Gorodetsky, Lichtman and Wong that $f_k = 1 - 2^{-k}(a_1 k^2 + O(k \log(k+1)))$. We prove that $f_k < f_{k+1}$ for every $k \geq 6$, and that $g_k > g_{k+1}$ for every $k \geq 1$. The two statements come from one analytic distinction. Writing $\sum_k P_k(s) z^k = ζ(s)^z H(s,z)$, at $s=1$ the point $z=2$ lies on the first singular circle of $H$, and strictly inside the first singular circle of the product with the prime $2$ removed. We show that this distinction decides the direction in general. If the complement of a set of primes $\mathcal{P}$ is thin and its least element is at least $3$, the corresponding sums eventually decrease, so the second theorem is one case of a general phenomenon. The inequalities used at the last step of the first theorem are certified by interval arithmetic.

title: Ranks of fibers in random elliptic surfaces
summary: For random integer polynomials $P$ of arbitrary degree we prove that for $100\%$ of elliptic surfaces $y^2=x^3-P(t)^2x$ the average 2-Selmer rank of the fibers is 3. Consequently, for $100\%$ these random elliptic surfaces we establish a lower bound for the proportion of fibers attaining algebraic rank $0$ and $1$.

title: A rank-zero $2$-converse to the Gross--Zagier and Kolyvagin theorem for elliptic curves with abelian two-division field
summary: Let $E/\mathbb{Q}$ be an elliptic curve with abelian two-division field. We prove that finiteness of ${\mathrm Sel}_{2^\infty}(E/\mathbb{Q})$ implies $L(E,1)\ne0$. The proof follows the quadratic twist deformation approach of OpenAI: Beilinson--Kato elements are interpolated over the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_2$-extension and over families of quadratic twists, and congruences in the resulting group ring transfer non-vanishing from the twists to $E$. The integral control of this interpolation is governed by one cohomological $μ$-invariant, which depends only on $E[2]$ and vanishes for abelian two-division fields. Together with Kato's cyclotomic divisibility and the fixed lattice in his construction, it bounds the denominator by a fixed power of $2$, independently of the twisting primes and the family dimension. Congruences among coefficients of a half-integral-weight form, in the style of Ono--Skinner, construct the required twist families.

title: On the $Δ$-primitive squares conjecture
summary: A natural number $n$ has the $Δ$ property if some difference of complementary divisors of $n$ is the sum of two such differences; equivalently, if some split graph has a factor graph containing an $n$-simple triangle. In additive terms, $n$ has the $Δ$ property exactly when the positive part of the factor-difference set of $n$, introduced by Erdős and Rosenfeld, is not sum-free. The set $\mathbb{N}(Δ)$ of such numbers is closed under multiplication by squares, and it was conjectured that it contains infinitely many $Δ$-primitive perfect squares. We prove this conjecture, and show that these squares can be chosen to avoid any prescribed finite set of primes but $3$.

title: $C_{\st}$-conjecture for compactly supported pro-étale cohomology
summary: We prove the étale-de Rham direction of the $C_{\st}$-conjecture for compactly supported cohomology of smooth partially proper rigid analytic varieties over local fields of mixed characteristic. More precisely, we recover filtered de Rham cohomology and (under a finite-rank assumption) Hyodo--Kato cohomology from compactly supported $p$-adic pro-étale cohomology as derived Hom (in a category of Arithmetic Topological Vector Spaces) with values in $\B_{\pdr}$ and $\B_{\pFF}$ respectively (period rings related to $\B_{\dr}$ and $\B_{\st}$ whose higher Galois cohomology vanishes). The proof uses, via the geometrized basic comparison theorem, Poincaré duality for Hyodo--Kato and (filtered) de Rham cohomology, explicit extension calculations for period sheaves, and fully-faithfulness of the passage from Galois equivariant perfect complexes on the Fargues--Fontaine curve to Arithmetic Topological Vector Spaces.

title: Simple algebraic groups with good reduction, the genus problem, and unramified cohomology
summary: We obtain a number of new results on the arithmetic of linear algebraic groups over higher-dimensional fields. In particular, we resolve some key open questions over 2-dimensional global fields, such as the finiteness of the genus of spinor groups of quadratic forms of dimension $\geq 10$. We also extend various finiteness results to new classes of fields, including function fields of $p$-adic surfaces. Our arguments rely in a crucial way on new finiteness results for unramified cohomology.

title: An Analytic Evaluation of Euler Sharp Sums
summary: We give a direct analytic evaluation of the Euler sharp sums $ζ^\sharp(2,\{1\}^{d-3},\overline{2})$ for all even integers $d\ge4$, expressing them in terms of ordinary multiple zeta values of depth at most two. The proof reduces these sharp sums to a harmonic-number series and evaluates it using a generating-function identity, thereby proving the even-depth case of a conjecture of Xu and Zhao.

title: Super-positivity via Dirichlet theta functions
summary: Let $χ$ be a quadratic Dirichlet character and let $Λ(χ, s)$ be its associated completed $L$-function. The super-positivity property, introduced by Yun--Zhang (2017), asserts that $Λ^{(m)} \left( \frac{1}{2}, χ\right) \geq 0$ for all $m \geq 0$. We show that a certain positivity property of its Dirichlet theta function $θ(t, χ)$, namely that $θ(t, χ)>0$ for all $t \geq 1$, implies the super-positivity property for $χ$. We then investigate a refined form of the above property: we conjecture that the sequence $\{ Λ^{(2m)}\left(\frac{1}{2}, χ\right )\}_{ m \geq 0}$ is always eventually increasing and has at most one turning point, and we prove these assertions again when $θ(t, χ)>0$ for $t \geq 1$.

title: Linear disjointness and values of Mahler M-functions
summary: We prove that the algebra generated by the values of Mahler M-functions at algebraic points admits a decomposition as the tensor product, over Q, of a countable family of linearly disjoint algebras. Consequently, the study of linear and algebraic relations among such values reduces to the corresponding problem within each of these smaller algebras. Our proof relies on recent advances of the authors on Mahler's method in several variables. As an application, we obtain a complete description of the algebraic relations among the values of the Fredholm series and their derivatives at nonzero algebraic points. This fully resolves an old problem originating in Mahler's work.

title: Nontrivial Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function and Its Derivative
summary: The nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function lie at the heart of analytic number theory. Through the explicit formulas, they govern the distribution of prime numbers: the closer all nontrivial zeros lie to the critical line $\Re(s)=\frac12$, the more uniformly the primes are distributed. The Riemann Hypothesis-asserting that all nontrivial zeros satisfy $\Re(s)=\frac12$-is equivalent to the optimal error bound $O(\sqrt{x}\log x)$ in the Prime Number Theorem. Beyond number theory, the zeros of $ζ(s)$ and its derivative $ζ'(s)$ are deeply intertwined: the horizontal distribution of $ζ'$-zeros near the critical line encodes information about the spacing of consecutive $ζ$-zeros. This paper establishes some results concerning the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function.

title: An asymptotic formula for primes of the form $u^2+v^2+1$
summary: We prove Motohashi's conjecture on primes of the form $u^2+v^2+1$, with Iwaniec's corrected constant. Let $b$ denote the characteristic function of the positive integers representable as a sum of two squares. Then, as $x\to\infty$, \[ \sum_{p\le x}b(p-1) =κ\Spr\frac{x}{(\log x)^{3/2}} +O\!\left(\frac{x}{(\log x)^{3/2}\sqrt{\log\log x}}\right), \] where $κ$ is the Landau--Ramanujan constant and $\Spr=\prod_{p\equiv3\,({\rm mod}\,4)}\bigl(1-1/(p(p-1))\bigr)$. The proof combines auxiliary prime factors with a mean square estimate for bilinear sums. We obtain the minor arc bound through harmonic switching and high moments, replacing arithmetic divisibility conditions by independent projective lines. We remove the auxiliary weights using Selberg's sieve.

title: Horizontal estimates for Kloosterman sums under Hecke eigenvalue constraints
summary: We prove weighted cancellation under small-value conditions on Hecke eigenvalues of finitely many non-CM holomorphic newforms. We also obtain many squarefree integers of each sign with fixed normalized amplitude, simultaneously small Hecke eigenvalues, and a fixed bound on the number of prime factors, uniformly in growing reduced residue classes. Our questions are motivated by Xi's noncorrelation conjectures and the mixed-moment estimates of Jiang and Lau. Their estimates imply that small Hecke eigenvalues can occur together with non-small Kloosterman values. Our result retains this property with a fixed prime-factor bound, both signs, and the residue conditions. Using OpenAI's zero-free half-plane theorem for Dirichlet $L$-functions, we give an example with at most $83$ prime factors, normalized amplitude at least $10^{-21}$, and moduli $M\le C^{11/200}$.

title: Ternary quadratic genera and generalized Hurwitz class numbers via quaternion orders
summary: We classify the genera of primitive positive definite ternary quadratic forms in the extremal cases of Lehman's level and discriminant conditions. The genera are parametrized by their level, discriminant, and genus conductor, which also distinguishes local forms having the same isotropy. Using the correspondence with quaternion orders of level $(N_1,N_2)$, we express their weighted representation numbers and class numbers in terms of generalized modified Hurwitz class numbers. The formulas allow arbitrary admissible prime power exponents and include the additional genera obtained by Watson's transformation. As an application, we determine all $255$ one-class genera in these families and give an explicit representation formula for each. Of these formulas, $110$ concern nonsquarefree $N_1N_2$.

title: Independence of Hasse--Weil $L$-functions over rings of Dirichlet series
summary: We study linear and algebraic independence of Hasse--Weil $L$-functions of abelian varieties over $\mathbb{Q}$, with Dirichlet series as coefficients. For nonzero varieties that are pairwise non-isogenous over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, we prove that their $L$-functions with arbitrary Dirichlet twists, together with all their derivatives and $1$, are linearly independent when the coefficient series use only primes from a set of natural density zero. For untwisted $L$-functions, this independence is equivalent to the condition that the varieties are pairwise non-isogenous over $\mathbb{Q}$. If the individual monodromy groups are connected, the result for varieties that are pairwise non-isogenous over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ extends to larger coefficient rings: the prime supports of coefficients are unrestricted outside a prescribed set of positive upper natural density and meet it in a set of natural density zero. We also characterize algebraic independence of untwisted $L$-functions in terms of the multiplicities of the simple isogeny factors of the varieties. The proofs combine an arithmetic-function lemma of Kaczorowski--Molteni--Perelli with Frobenius density arguments and require no analytic continuation or automorphy.

title: A relative trace formula for the orthogonal Gan-Gross-Prasad model and the proof of its fundamental lemma
summary: In this paper, we propose a comparison of relative trace formulas to study the Gan--Gross--Prasad conjecture. We unfold the relative trace formulas, match their regular orbits, and formulate the corresponding fundamental lemma and smooth transfer conjecture. Finally, we prove the fundamental lemma for the unit element of the Hecke algebra.

title: On the higher-order Titchmarsh divisor problem
summary: For every fixed integer $k\geq2$ and every fixed nonzero integer $h$, we prove that, as $x\to\infty$, \begin{equation*} \sum_{x<n\leq2x}Λ(n)τ_k(n+h) \sim C_{k,h}x(\log x)^{k-1}, \end{equation*} where $τ_k$ is the $k$-fold divisor function and $C_{k,h}>0$ is a constant depending only on $k$ and $h$.

title: Why the non-abelian Gyarmati--Matolcsi--Ruzsa inequality does not generally work: mechanisms and explicit examples
summary: For finite sets in a commutative semigroup, Gyarmati, Matolcsi and Ruzsa proved \[ |A_1+\dots+A_n|^{n-1}\ \le\ \prod_{i=1}^n|A_1+\dots+A_{i-1}+A_{i+1}+\dots+A_n| . \] They asked whether in an arbitrary group \[ |A_1\cdots A_n|^{n-1}\ \le\ \prod_{i=1}^n\ \max_{a\in A_i}\,|A_1\cdots A_{i-1}\,a\,A_{i+1}\cdots A_n| , \] where each omitted set is replaced by the largest slice obtained by fixing one of its elements. Nair, Namayandeh and Zhu proved that this inequality does not hold when $n=4$ and $G=D_4^{14}$, of group order $8^{14}$. We develop its double-coset mechanism and construct counterexamples in many other groups. For $n=4$, the smallest group found has order $518\,400$, namely $A_6^2\times C_2^2$; no absolute minimality is claimed. For $n=6$ there is a witness in a group of order $1728$, for $n=10$ a class-three $3$-group of order $243$ suffices, and for $n=4$ a single class-two $2$-group of order $2^{23}$ works. We also obtain torsion-free examples. The violation ratio $R_n=|A_1\cdots A_n|^{n-1}/\prod_iN_i$ is greater than one exactly when the inequality fails; explicit four-set constructions attain $R_4\approx1.29$ in $A_8^2$, and a larger ratio of about $1.43$ is reported for $A_{10}^2$. For every $n\ge4$, the inequality holds in all direct powers of $G$ precisely when $G$ is abelian. For $n\ge2$ the optimal exponent $θ_n$ is the infimum of $\log(\prod_iN_i)/\log|A_1\cdots A_n|$ over products of size at least two. We obtain $2\leθ_n\le n-1.0768$, and an infinite family in $C_3*C_3$ shows $θ_n\le n-1-δ$ for every $δ<5-2\log_25\approx0.3561$ and all sufficiently large $n$.

title: A complete symmetric rank-two modularity classification, obtained through a sharp uniform degree bound
summary: We classify modular Nahm sums with a rational symmetric positive-definite two-by-two matrix and rational shifts. Up to coordinate exchange, every modular datum belongs to three explicit rational-point families, is a product of two modular rank-one sums, or is one of thirty-four exceptional triples on twelve matrices. The list consists of Zagier's rank-two examples, the Vlasenko--Zwegers additions and split products; no further data occur. The proof first bounds the joint degree of the distinguished Nahm point by four, using an initial degree bound of twenty-four and exact local exclusions at the prime 7. Explicit height and exponent bounds then give exhaustive arithmetic classifications in degrees one through four. Exact polynomial elimination determines all rational shifts, and published identities of q-series establish modularity of the survivors. The degree bound is sharp. The finite steps are accompanied by exact certificates, verification programs and independently implemented checks. Computational companion: https://github.com/johnngy44/math/releases

title: Spectral gaps and mixing rates of primitive matrices
summary: We obtain lower bounds on spectral gap/upper bounds for mixing rate for arbitrary $n$-state (not necessarily reversible) primitive Markov chains which have exponent $-O(n)$ rather than $-O(n^2)$, a significant improvement on the order obtained from classical arguments. Our improvements come from using the irreducibility distance and chainable index (which are at most linear in $n$) rather than the primitivity index (which can be near $n^2$). This also yields corresponding bounds for arbitrary nonnegative primitive matrices.

title: Phase Transitions for Random Least Common Multiples with Memory
summary: We study the least common multiple of a random subset of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ when the selection follows a correlated Bernoulli process with memory. The copying rule preserves the marginal retention probabilities and creates a genealogical forest. At fixed density, the logarithmic least common multiple exhibits a fluctuation phase transition at the memory parameter $a=1/2$. The boundary limits depend on how genealogical families are distributed among the divisibility classes carrying the leading arithmetic weight. Our proofs combine the von Mangoldt representation with a reduction to large primes. At fixed density, an exact expansion separates an innovation martingale from a memory term. An asymptotic projection onto the retained count identifies the contribution of memory. Marked point-process convergence and estimates for rare genealogical families give the boundary limits.

title: Probabilistic counting of labelled trees with prescribed vertical edge profile
summary: The vertical edge profile of a labelled plane tree $t$ is the collection of integers counting the number of oriented edges from label $i$ to label $j$ for every possible pairs of labels $(i, j)$. In a previous work by the second author, it was shown that a process constructed from the vertical edge profile forms a Markov chain for a wide class of models of random labelled plane trees where edge label increments are constrained to lie in $\{-1, 0, 1\}$. The purpose of this paper is twofold. First, we continue the study of Markov properties of the vertical edge profile. In particular, we derive general formulas for the transition kernel and the initial distribution of a class of Markov chains related to the vertical edge profile. Second, we apply these results to the probabilistic enumeration of trees with a prescribed vertical edge profile. These applications yield a unified probabilistic derivation of several enumeration formulas. In particular, we recover some results established Bousquet-Mélou and Chapuy for binary trees and Cayley trees. These enumeration formulas admit a remarkable factorized form, already noted in previous works. The probabilistic methods developed here explain this phenomenon by showing that these factorizations arise naturally from the Markov structure underlying the vertical edge profile.

title: Higher properties T and finiteness properties for twin building lattices
summary: Properties $[T_k]$ and finiteness properties $FP_k(\mathbb{Q})$ and $F_k$ are refinements of the following fundamental notions for groups: Kazhdan property T in the first case, and finite generation/presentation in the last two cases. Under suitable hypotheses on the thickness, we prove that every twin building lattice of $(k+1)$-spherical type $(W,S)$, where $k\geq 1$, has property $[T_k]$ and is of type $FP_k(\mathbb{Q})$. If $(W,S)$ is classical, that group is even of type $F_k$. To the best of the author's knowledge, this produces the first examples of infinite finitely presented simple groups with property $[T_k]$ for some $k\geq 2$, and the first examples of finitely presented simple Kazhdan groups that are Frobenius stable and not Frobenius approximable. Along the way, we establish new criteria for property $[T_k]$ for groups acting on CW complexes that extend results of Dymara--Januszkiewicz and Grinbaum-Reizis--Oppenheim. As a key step in our proofs, we determine high acyclicity and, in classical type, high connectivity properties for the opposite complex of a Moufang twin building of $(k+1)$-spherical type and suitable finite thickness.

title: Automorphism of reduced finitary power monoids
summary: Let $H$ be a multiplicatively written monoid with identity element $1_H$. The family $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin},1}(H)$ of all finite subsets of $H$ containing $1_H$ is a monoid with identity $\{1_H\}$ under the setwise multiplication induced by $H$. We prove that $\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin},1}(H)) \cong \operatorname{Aut}(H)$ whenever $H$ satisfies either of the following two conditions: (1) $H$ is commutative, cancellative, and contains an invertible element of infinite order; (2) $H$ is an abelian group which is not isomorphic to the Klein four-group.

title: Marginal Congruences and Elements for Two Commutator Words in Completely Regular Semigroups
summary: Motivated by Problem 13 posed by Araújo, Araújo and Kinyon \cite{Araujo2025} concerning marginal elements, subsemigroups and marginal equivalences associated with commutator words in completely regular semigroups, in this paper we investigate the two commutator words $ ω_1(x,y)=x^{-1}y^{-1}xy$ and $ ω_2(x,y)=(yx)^{-1}xy$ on completely regular semigroups. We prove that their marginal equivalences $\sim_{ω_r}$ ($r=1,2$) coincide and are congruences. More precisely, for a completely regular semigroup $S$, we show that $a\sim_{ω_r}b$ ($r=1,2$) if and only if $a^0=b^0=p$ and $b^{-1}a\in Z(pSp)$, where $Z(pSp)$ is the center of the monoid $pSp$, and so both words have the same set of marginal elements: \[ M_ω(S) =\bigcup_{p\in E(S)} \bigl(Z(pSp)\cap H_p\bigr), \] where $E(S)$ is the set of idempotents in $S$. We also characterize when this set is a subsemigroup and establish alternative descriptions of the common marginal congruence and marginal elements.

title: A novel Non-Homogeneous Local Representation of the Braid Group
summary: We construct a non-homogeneous local representation of the braid group $B_n$ by tracking the labels of individual strands through successive crossings. Each generator acts through a $2\times2$ block whose position is determined by the crossing and whose coefficients depend on the ordered labels of the participating strands. Starting with the ansatz \[ M_{xy}=\begin{pmatrix}a_x&a_y\\ b_{xy}&c_{xy}\end{pmatrix}, \] for $n\geq3$, the cubic braid relations for arbitrary ordered triples of strands determine $c_{xy}=0$ and $b_{xy}=(1-a_x)/a_x$ in the nondegenerate branch. The moving-label rule leads to an explicit semidirect-product representation, for which we prove the Artin relations and use exact evaluations of the resulting symbolic matrices. In the special homogeneous specialization, where $a_x=a$ for every strand label $x$, the resulting matrix representation is diagonally equivalent to unreduced Burau. We prove that a non-homogeneous specialization of our representation detects Bigelow's explicit nontrivial $B_5$ Burau-kernel commutator. Thus the strand-dependent coefficients distinguish a nontrivial braid that is invisible to the classical Burau representation. This separation provides evidence that the non-homogeneous strand-tracking construction is a promising candidate for a faithful Burau-type representation.

title: The Herzog--Schönheim Conjecture for Solvable Groups
summary: The Herzog--Schönheim conjecture states that if a group is partitioned into finitely many, and at least two, cosets of subgroups, then two of these subgroups have the same index. We prove the conjecture for all solvable groups, finite or infinite. Sun's bound on unions of cosets, applied in a quotient, is combined with divisibility restrictions on local indices relative to the subgroup generated by the $p$-elements, where $p$ is the largest prime divisor of the order of a minimal counterexample. These restrictions are obtained by counting fixed points in a primitive solvable quotient. This suffices except at the prime $7$, where the counting bound narrowly fails and an additional overlap argument is needed. The proof has been formalized in Lean~4 with mathlib.

title: Property $R_\infty$ for Higman$\unicode{x2013}$Thompson Groups
summary: We prove that every Higman$\unicode{x2013}$Thompson group $G_{n,r}$, with $n\ge2$ and $r\ge1$, has property $R_\infty$. In particular, every automorphism of Thompson's group $V = G_{2,1}$ has infinitely many twisted conjugacy classes. These results answer questions of Olukoya and of Lins de Araujo, de Oliveira-Tosti and Santos Rego. We also prove that a homeomorphism under which no eventually periodic sequence has a finite orbit has a locally finite centralizer in $G_{n,r}$.

title: Finite soluble groups with Sylow subgroups of class at most two are IYB-groups
summary: We prove that every finite soluble group whose Sylow subgroups have nilpotency class at most two is an involutive Yang--Baxter group ($\IYB$-group). This answers a question of Cedó and Okniński \cite{CedoOkninski2025}. The main method of the $\IYB$-structures has been reflected in \cite{MengBallesterJimenez2026}.

title: The cohomology of finite simple groups is unbounded
summary: In every fixed positive degree, we show that the cohomology of finite simple groups, algebraic groups and quantum groups, with coefficients in simple modules, can have arbitrarily large dimension. In particular, we disprove Guralnick's conjecture.

title: Group cosets with all elements automorphically equivalent
summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and let $N$ be a proper non-trivial normal subgroup of $G$. We say that $(G,N)$ is an \textit{automorphically equivalent pair} if for every element $x\in G\setminus N$, the elements in the coset $xN$ belong to the same orbit under the action of ${\rm Aut}(G)$. This generalizes the concept of a Camina pair and constitutes a particular type of equal order pair. In this note, we determine all automorphically equivalent pairs in the class of finite abelian groups.

title: Schur multiplier exponents of finite $p$-groups: bounds and critical-class phenomena
summary: The Schur exponent conjecture is a long-standing conjecture in group theory, which asserts that $\operatorname{exp}(\mathrm{M}(G))\mid\operatorname{exp}(G)$ for every finite group $G$, where $\mathrm{M}(G)$ denotes the Schur multiplier of $G$. In this article, we prove that the Schur exponent conjecture holds for finite $p$-groups $G$ of nilpotency class at most $2p-2$ when $p$ is an odd prime. Our approach is to establish upper bounds on the exponent of $γ_{s+1}(G)$ for $s\in\mathbb{N}$. Using this approach, we further establish exponent bounds for Schur multipliers, nonabelian exterior squares, and tensor squares of $G$ of arbitrary nilpotency class, improving some existing bounds. Moreover, we show that Moravec's Bogomolov multiplier exponent conjecture holds for finite $p$-groups of nilpotency class at most $2p-1$. Havas conjectured that, for every prime $p>3$, there exists a finite $p$-group of exponent $p$ and nilpotency class $2p-1$ for which the Schur exponent conjecture fails. We show that the Schur exponent conjecture still holds for finite $p$-groups of nilpotency class at most $2p-1$ generated by at most three elements. For four-generator groups of exponent $p$ and class at most $2p-1$, we prove that $\mathrm{M}(G)\cong C_{p^2}^{\,b}\times C_p^{\,a}$ for some $a\ge0$ and $b\in\{0,1\}$.

title: Extreme amenability and failure of the Lévy property for the trace-class special unitary group
summary: We prove that the trace-class special unitary group, equipped with the trace-norm topology, is extremely amenable but is not a Lévy group, answering questions posed by Pestov. The failure of the Lévy property follows from a uniform non-concentration estimate for every nontrivial compact subgroup. Extreme amenability is established through a transverse spectral-gap estimate and trace-norm duality, yielding asymptotic invariance of Lipschitz observables under each fixed finite-dimensional special unitary subgroup. A limiting argument then gives fixed points for continuous actions on arbitrary compact Hausdorff spaces. We also formulate an abstract criterion for extreme amenability based on asymptotic quadratic invariance along a dense chain of compact subgroups. Neither argument uses concentration results for other Schatten exponents.

title: Integrable Measure Equivalence and Gromov's conjecture on nilpotent groups
summary: In this article we prove a well-known conjecture due to M. Gromov that if two infinite finitely generated torsion free nilpotent groups $Γ$ and $Λ$ are Quasi-isometric, then their Mal'cev Completions are isomorphic as Lie groups. We prove this result in more general set-up. We prove that if two infinite finitely generated torsion free nilpotent groups $Γ$ and $Λ$ are Integrable Measure Equivalent, then the Mal'cev completions of $Γ$ and $Λ$ are isomorphic as Lie groups. Equivalently, using Y. Shalom's result we prove that two infinite countable torsion free nilpotent groups $Γ$ and $Λ$ are Integrable Measure Equivalent if and only if $Γ$ and $Λ$ are quasi-isometric if and only if the Mal'cev Completions of $Γ$ and $Λ$ are isomorphic as Lie groups. Moreover, we discuss some applications of our main theorem to lifting of quasi-isometric embedding from $Γ$ to $Λ$ to a homo-morphism between their Mal'cev completions, and betti numbers of nilpotent groups.

title: Gorenstein modules over Thompson's group
summary: Let $k$ be any commutative ring of characteristic $0$. We construct an example of a countably presented Gorenstein projective module over the algebra of Thompson's group $F$ with coefficients in $k$, that is not Benson cofibrant. In particular, we provide a negative answer to a conjecture proposed by Dembegioti and Talelli. The construction uses a general method that produces totally acyclic complexes of flat modules and is based on the computation of the (co-)cohomology of $F$ by Brown and Geoghegan.

title: Strong pseudo Frobenius numbers
summary: By Sylow's theorem, the number of Sylow $p$-subgroups of a finite group is congruent to $1$ modulo $p$, but not every such integer occurs. Frobenius extended the congruence to the number of subgroups of order $p^a$ for every $a\ge0$. Kulakoff and Hall showed that this number is congruent to $1$ or $1+p$ modulo $p^2$ whenever $p^{a+1}$ divides the group order. A positive integer is a Frobenius $p$-number if it is the number of subgroups of order $p^a$ of some finite group for some $a$. There are integers congruent to $1$ modulo $p^2$ which are not Frobenius $p$-numbers, and it remained open whether there are also such integers congruent to $1+p$ modulo $p^2$. We show that no finite group has exactly $106$ subgroups of order $5^a$ for any $a\ge0$.
